name: Cloud Lobe
description:
Cloud refers to a network of remote servers that store, manage, and process data and applications, providing on-demand access and scalable computing resources over the internet.

The Cloud lobe of the Digital Reference ontology models AH Local Cloud, Communication Technology, Data Format and Model, Device, and Documentation Document.
It also maps the topics of Information Model, Local Network, Method, SoA Property, Software and Software System, system Documentation and System of Systems.
It represents the notion of  Service, Service Documentation, Service-Oriented Architecture and Architecture Protocols.

subclasses.name: Software
subclasses.description: The class Software represents a series of computer instructions that tell the computer how to operate and execute specific tasks.

subclasses.name: Application System Type
subclasses.description: An application system type classifies individual application systems which have exactly the same technological properties. Process steps might be supported by application systems. Object describe IT systems (library for IT systems available).

subclasses.name: AH Device
subclasses.description: A device in the context of Arrowhead framework is a piece of equipment, machine, hardware, etc. with computational, memory, and communication capabilities which hosts one or several Arrowhead Framework systems. (Source: Arrowhead)

subclasses.name: Constrained Device
subclasses.description:
A constrained device is a device in the sense of an service-oriented architecture that is restricted in terms of processing capabilities (speed, complexity of operations), memory and power supply.
The concept constrained device was introduced in the context of the Internet of Things (IoT) and refers for example to sensor devices, location devices, switches etc. which are connected by low-power wireless communication technologies like BLE, ZigBee, Z-Wave etc., have a battery on board that should last for two to three years and which are (very) small in physical size.

subclasses.name: Illumination Device
subclasses.description: A category of devices which's purpose is to illuminate

subclasses.name: Sensor Device
subclasses.description: A category of devices which's purpose is to sense

subclasses.name: Switch Device
subclasses.description: A switch is a device in a computer network that connects other devices together.

subclasses.name: Gateway
subclasses.description: A gateway is a piece of networking hardware used in telecommunications for telecommunications networks that allows data to flow from one discrete network to another.

subclasses.name: Industrial Personal Computer
subclasses.description: Industrial PCs are primarily used for process control and/or data acquisition. In some cases, an industrial PC is simply used as a front-end to another control computer in a distributed processing environment.

subclasses.name: Personal Computer
subclasses.description: A personal computer (PC) is a multi-purpose computer whose size, capabilities, and price make it feasible for individual use.

subclasses.name: Programmable Logic Controller
subclasses.description: A programmable logic controller (PLC) is an industrial digital computer which has been ruggedized and adapted for the control of manufacturing processes

subclasses.name: Raspberry Pi
subclasses.description: The Raspberry Pi is a series of small single-board computers developed in the United Kingdom by the Raspberry Pi Foundation to put the power of computing and digital making into the hands of people all over the world.

subclasses.name: Smartphone
subclasses.description: A smartphone is a mobile device that combines cellular and mobile computing functions into one unit.

subclasses.name: Tablet Computer
subclasses.description: A tablet computer, commonly shortened to tablet, is a mobile device, typically with a mobile operating system and touchscreen display

subclasses.name: AH Local Cloud
subclasses.description: AH Local Cloud is a subclass of Cloud Lobe representing a self-contained, private digital environment set up within a specific physical location, such as a factory floor or industrial site. It groups together a collection of connected software systems and devices that need to work with one another, and must always include three essential built-in components: a service directory so systems can find each other, an access control system so only permitted systems can communicate, and a coordination system so the right systems are matched to the right tasks.

subclasses.name: Communication Technology
subclasses.description: Communications technology, also known as information technology, refers to all equipment and programs that are used to process and communicate information.

subclasses.name: Communication Security Mechanism
subclasses.description: corresponds to a part of OSI layer 5

subclasses.name: Data Link Media Access Technology
subclasses.description: corresponds to OSI layer 1 and 2 technologies, like Ethernet, WLAN (802.11), WPAN (802.15.4), EtherCAT, ProfiNet, ...

subclasses.name: End To End Communication Technology
subclasses.description: The end-to-end principle is a design framework in computer networking. In networks designed according to this principle, application-specific features reside in the communicating end nodes of the network, rather than in intermediary nodes, such as gateways and routers, that exist to establish the network.

subclasses.name: Point To Point Communication Technology
subclasses.description: corresponds to OSI layer 3, e.g. IPv4 or IPv6

subclasses.name: Transfer Protocol
subclasses.description: corresponds to OSI layers 6 and 7

subclasses.name: Data Format
subclasses.description: Data format in information technology may refer to: Data type, constraint placed upon the interpretation of data in a type system.

subclasses.name: Data Model
subclasses.description: A data model is an abstract model that organizes elements of data and standardizes how they relate to one another and to the properties of real-world entities.

subclasses.name: Documentation Document
subclasses.description: A document that documents something

subclasses.name: AH Service Documentation Document
subclasses.description:
Document belonging to the documentation of an Arrowhead Service.
There are four types of documents for Arrowhead service documentations:
- Service Description
- Interface Design Description
- Communication Profile
- Semantic Profile.
The central documents are IDDs. They document the implementation of a certain service based on a certain communication technology (communication, encoding, data format) and a certain information model.
The Service Description contains a more general description of the service, without the link to a specific communication technology or information model.
Communication Profiles and Semantic Profiles are optional documents for a service documentation. They can be seen as modules of an IDD, since they can describe the communication technolopgy and the information model of a service implementation as external documents. If they exist, the IDD refers to them instead of declaring these contents by themselfes.
That is, CP and SP are useful if different service implementations use the same CP and SP - then their IDDs can refer to one and the same CP or SP document.

subclasses.name: Communication Profile CP
subclasses.description: Communication Profile (CP)

subclasses.name: Interface Design Description IDD
subclasses.description: Interface Design Description (IDD)

subclasses.name: AH Application Servcice IDD
subclasses.description: AH Application Service IDD (Application Service Interface Design Description) is a subclass of AH Service Documentation Document and represents the central document within the documentation set of a specific application service in the Eclipse Arrowhead Framework. As an Interface Design Description, it provides a complete and technically precise specification of a service implementation by defining the communication technology, encoding scheme, data format, and information model used by application systems that exchange information by providing and/or consuming application services. It may either declare these technical contents directly or reference external Communication Profile and Semantic Profile documents where those exist, making it the authoritative linking document between the general service description and all technology-specific implementation details.

subclasses.name: AH Core Service IDD
subclasses.description: AH Core Service IDD is a subclass of Interface Design Description IDD specifically covering the technical specification documents for the built-in services that keep the Arrowhead Framework running. These documents describe how each built-in service works, how other systems can interact with it, and what rules govern those interactions, forming the foundation that all other services in the network rely on.

subclasses.name: AH Automation Supporting Service IDD
subclasses.description: AH Automation Supporting Service IDD is a subclass of AH Core Service IDD representing technical specification documents for optional built-in services that extend the basic capabilities of an Arrowhead environment. Where the three essential built-in services handle only the minimum needed to get systems talking to each other, these additional services cover broader needs such as storing data, handling events, managing configurations, and monitoring quality, supporting more complete and capable automated operations.

subclasses.name: AH Device Discovery Service IDD
subclasses.description: AH Device Discovery Service IDD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting Service IDD representing the technical specification document for a service that automatically finds and registers physical devices, such as sensors, machines, or hardware components, within an Arrowhead environment. Once a device is identified and registered, it can be recognised and used by other systems in the network without needing manual configuration.

subclasses.name: AH Global Service Discovery Service IDD
subclasses.description: AH Global Service Discovery Service IDD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting Service IDD representing the technical specification document for a service that enables systems to find and access services located outside their own local environment. Rather than being limited to what is available within a single local network, this service allows a system to search for and connect with services in other locations or networks.

subclasses.name: AH Inter Cloud Negotiations Service IDD
subclasses.description: AH Inter Cloud Negotiations Service IDD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting Service IDD representing the technical specification document for a service that manages the process of establishing agreements and connections between two or more separate Arrowhead local environments. It handles the rules and steps that allow separate, independently managed networks to share resources and collaborate safely.

subclasses.name: AH Session Establish Service IDD
subclasses.description: AH Session Establish Service IDD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting Service IDD representing the technical specification document for a service that handles the process of starting a new communication session between two or more systems. It defines the steps and requirements needed before systems can begin exchanging information, ensuring that all parties are properly identified and that the connection is set up in a consistent and secure way.

subclasses.name: AH Session Management Service IDD
subclasses.description: AH Session Management Service IDD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting Service IDD representing the technical specification document for a service that oversees the full life of a communication session between systems, from the moment it begins, through its active use, until it is properly closed. It ensures that ongoing exchanges between systems remain orderly, trackable, and properly terminated when no longer needed.

subclasses.name: AH System Discovery Service IDD
subclasses.description: AH System Discovery Service IDD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting Service IDD representing the technical specification document for a service that finds and catalogues the software systems present within an Arrowhead environment. Rather than discovering physical devices, this service identifies and records the software systems and applications in the network, what they are, what they can do, and how they are configured, so that the broader network has an accurate and current picture of its members.

subclasses.name: AH Mandatory Core Service IDD
subclasses.description:
Class of all Interface Design Descriptions (IDDs) of mandatory Arrowhead core services.
While the class AH_mandatory_core_service contains the mandatory core services only as instances, this class contains classes of the IDDs of each single mandatory core service as subclasses (not only as instances). Since each AH Local Cloud runs one instance of each mandatory core service, each of these services has to be documented by an AH service documentation, i.e. at least by a SD and a IDD. So the IDD is an individual document for each mandatory core service in each single Local Cloud. Hence, all IDDs of a certain mandatory core service will be individuals of the corresponding IDD class.

subclasses.name: AH Authorization Control Service IDD
subclasses.description: AH Authorization Control Service IDD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core Service IDD representing the technical specification document for the service that controls who is allowed to access what within an Arrowhead local environment. It formally describes how the access control service works, including how it verifies identities and enforces permissions, ensuring that only approved systems can communicate with one another.

subclasses.name: AH Orchestration Service IDD
subclasses.description: AH Orchestration Service IDD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core Service IDD representing the technical specification document for the coordination service that is required in every Arrowhead local environment. This coordination service is responsible for deciding, at the moment a request is made, which available service a system should connect to, acting like a matchmaker that routes requests to the most appropriate provider. This document formally defines how that matching process works and the rules that govern it.

subclasses.name: AH Service Discovery Service IDD
subclasses.description: AH Service Discovery Service IDD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core Service IDD representing the technical specification document for the service directory lookup function required in every Arrowhead local environment. This function allows any system in the network to search for and find other services that are available, similar to looking up a contact in a directory. This document formally defines how that search and lookup process works.

subclasses.name: AH Store Management Service IDD
subclasses.description: AH Store Management Service IDD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core Service IDD representing the technical specification document for the service responsible for storing, organising, and retrieving data within an Arrowhead local environment. This service acts as the managed data store for the network, ensuring that information needed by systems is saved reliably and can be accessed when required.

subclasses.name: AH Token Generation Service IDD
subclasses.description: AH Token Generation Service IDD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core Service IDD representing the technical specification document for the service that issues security tokens within an Arrowhead local environment. A security token is a short-lived digital pass that a system presents to prove it has been granted permission to use a particular service, similar to a ticket that grants entry for a specific purpose. This document formally defines how those tokens are created and what they must contain.

subclasses.name: Semantic Profile SP
subclasses.description: Semantic Profile (SP)

subclasses.name: Service Description SD
subclasses.description: Service Description (SD)

subclasses.name: AH Application Service SD
subclasses.description: AH Application Service SD is a subclass of Service Description SD that provides a plain, general description of a specific application service, one built to address a particular real-world use case rather than to run the network itself. It describes what the service does and why it exists, without specifying technical implementation details, and serves as the starting point from which a full technical specification is developed.

subclasses.name: AH Core Service SD
subclasses.description: AH Core Service SD is a subclass of Service Description SD that provides plain, general descriptions of the built-in services that form the backbone of the Arrowhead Framework, both the essential ones and the optional supporting ones. These descriptions explain what each built-in service does and what role it plays, without going into technical implementation details.

subclasses.name: AH Automation Supporting Service SD
subclasses.description: AH Automation Supporting Service SD is a subclass of AH Core Service SD providing plain, general descriptions of optional built-in services that extend the Arrowhead Framework beyond its mandatory core, covering capabilities such as event handling, data management, session control, or device discovery. These descriptions explain the purpose and role of each supporting service without specifying technical implementation details.

subclasses.name: AH Device Discovery Service SD
subclasses.description: AH Device Discovery Service SD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting Service SD providing the plain, general description of the service that automatically finds and registers physical hardware devices, such as sensors and machines, within an Arrowhead environment. It explains the purpose and role of device discovery without specifying any technical implementation details.

subclasses.name: AH Global Service Discovery Service SD
subclasses.description: AH Global Service Discovery Service SD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting Service SD providing the plain, general description of the service that enables systems to search for and locate services available beyond their own local environment. It explains the cross-network discovery role of this service without specifying technical implementation details.

subclasses.name: AH Inter Cloud Negotiations Service SD
subclasses.description: AH Inter Cloud Negotiations Service SD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting Service SD providing the plain, general description of the service that establishes agreements and authorised connections between separate Arrowhead local environments. It explains the inter-cloud coordination role of this service without specifying technical implementation details.

subclasses.name: AH Session Establish Service SD
subclasses.description: AH Session Establish Service SD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting Service SD providing the plain, general description of the service that handles the initiation of communication sessions between systems, explaining how participating systems are identified and how sessions are started, without specifying technical implementation details.

subclasses.name: AH Session Management Service SD
subclasses.description: AH Session Management Service SD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting Service SD providing the plain, general description of the service that oversees the complete lifecycle of communication sessions between systems, from initiation through active use to orderly termination, without specifying technical implementation details.

subclasses.name: AH System Discovery Service SD
subclasses.description: AH System Discovery Service SD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting Service SD providing the plain, general description of the service that finds and catalogues the software systems present in an Arrowhead environment. It explains the role of this service in maintaining an accurate and current registry of active network members, without specifying technical implementation details.

subclasses.name: AH Mandatory Core Service SD
subclasses.description: AH Mandatory Core Service SD is a subclass of AH Core Service SD covering plain, general descriptions specifically for the three services that must be present in every Arrowhead local environment: the service directory, the access control system, and the coordination system. Without these three, the network cannot function, making their descriptions a foundational part of the overall documentation.

subclasses.name: AH Authorization Control Service SD
subclasses.description: AH Authorization Control Service SD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core Service SD providing the plain, general description of the access control service that must be present in every Arrowhead local environment. This service is responsible for deciding which systems are allowed to communicate with which other systems, ensuring that no system can access a service it has not been explicitly permitted to use, and that every system is who it claims to be before any exchange takes place.

subclasses.name: AH Orchestration Service SD
subclasses.description: AH Orchestration Service SD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core Service SD providing the plain, general description of the coordination service required in every Arrowhead local environment. It explains the role of this service in dynamically matching service consumer requests to the most appropriate service providers at runtime, without specifying technical implementation details.

subclasses.name: AH Service Discovery Service SD
subclasses.description: AH Service Discovery Service SD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core Service SD providing the plain, general description of the service directory lookup function required in every Arrowhead local environment. It explains how this service enables any system in the network to search for and find other services that are currently available and registered.

subclasses.name: AH Store Management Service SD
subclasses.description: AH Store Management Service SD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core Service SD providing the plain, general description of the service responsible for storing, organising, and retrieving data within an Arrowhead local environment. It explains the managed data store role of this service, making stored information reliably accessible to other systems in the network.

subclasses.name: AH Token Generation Service SD
subclasses.description: AH Token Generation Service SD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core Service SD providing the plain, general description of the service that issues secure authorisation tokens granting a service consumer time- or scope-limited permission to consume a provider's service. It explains the token-based access-control role of this service within the mandatory security functionality of an Arrowhead local environment, without specifying technical implementation details.

subclasses.name: AH System Documentation Document
subclasses.description: AH System Documentation Document is a subclass of Documentation Document representing any formal document produced as part of the documentation of a software system within the Arrowhead Framework. These documents collectively describe a system from both external and internal perspectives, covering what it does and how it is designed, providing the information needed to understand, implement, and integrate it.

subclasses.name: System Description Sy SD
subclasses.description: System Description Sy SD is a subclass of AH System Documentation Document providing a plain, technology-independent description of a software system from an external perspective, explaining what services it provides and consumes and the role it plays within the broader system of systems, without detailing internal design or implementation choices.

subclasses.name: AH Application System Sy SD
subclasses.description: AH Application System Sy SD is a subclass of System Description Sy SD providing the plain, external description of an Arrowhead application system, explaining what the system does, which services it provides and consumes, and its role in the system of systems, without specifying internal design or implementation details.

subclasses.name: AH Core System Sy SD
subclasses.description: AH Core System Sy SD is a subclass of System Description Sy SD providing the plain, external description of an Arrowhead core system, applicable to both mandatory and automation supporting core systems, explaining the system's role and its service interactions within the local cloud without detailing internal implementation.

subclasses.name: AH Automation Supporting System Sy SD
subclasses.description: AH Automation Supporting System Sy SD is a subclass of AH Core System Sy SD providing the plain, external description of an Arrowhead automation supporting system, one of the optional built-in systems that extends the mandatory core with additional capabilities, explaining its role and service interactions within the local cloud without specifying internal implementation details.

subclasses.name: AH Device Registry System Sy SD
subclasses.description: AH Device Registry System Sy SD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting System Sy SD providing the plain, external description of the Device Registry System, an optional core system that maintains a record of physical hardware devices registered within an Arrowhead environment, explaining its role and service interactions without internal implementation detail.

subclasses.name: AH Gatekeeper System Sy SD
subclasses.description: AH Gatekeeper System Sy SD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting System Sy SD providing the plain, external description of the Gatekeeper System, an optional core system responsible for negotiating and controlling access between separate Arrowhead local environments, explaining its inter-cloud coordination role without internal implementation detail.

subclasses.name: AH Gateway System Sy SD
subclasses.description: AH Gateway System Sy SD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting System Sy SD providing the plain, external description of the Gateway System, an optional core system that relays data between separate Arrowhead local environments once inter-cloud access has been negotiated, explaining its role and service interactions without internal implementation detail.

subclasses.name: AH Historian Sy SD
subclasses.description: AH Historian Sy SD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting System Sy SD providing the plain, external description of the Historian system, an optional core system that records and stores historical operational data from the local environment for retrospective analysis and traceability, without specifying internal implementation detail.

subclasses.name: AH QoS Manager Sy SD
subclasses.description: AH QoS Manager Sy SD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting System Sy SD providing the plain, external description of the Quality of Service Manager system, an optional core system that monitors and manages the performance and reliability characteristics of service exchanges within the local environment.

subclasses.name: AH System Registry System Sy SD
subclasses.description: AH System Registry System Sy SD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting System Sy SD providing the plain, external description of the System Registry system, an optional core system that catalogues the software systems active within an Arrowhead environment to support system-level discovery and management.

subclasses.name: AH Mandatory Core System Sy SD
subclasses.description: AH Mandatory Core System Sy SD is a subclass of AH Core System Sy SD providing the plain, external description of one of the three mandatory core systems required in every Arrowhead local environment, covering the Service Registry, Orchestrator, and Authorization systems, each explained in terms of its essential role and service interactions without specifying internal design.

subclasses.name: AH Authorization System Sy SD
subclasses.description: AH Authorization System Sy SD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core System Sy SD providing the plain, external description of the Authorization System, one of the three mandatory core systems in every Arrowhead local environment, explaining its role in enforcing access control between communicating systems without specifying internal design.

subclasses.name: AH Orchestration System Sy SD
subclasses.description: AH Orchestration System Sy SD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core System Sy SD providing the plain, external description of the Orchestration System, one of the three mandatory core systems in every Arrowhead local environment, explaining its role in dynamically matching service consumer requests to appropriate service providers at runtime.

subclasses.name: AH Service Registry System Sy SD
subclasses.description: AH Service Registry System Sy SD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core System Sy SD providing the plain, external description of the Service Registry System, one of the three mandatory core systems in every Arrowhead local environment, explaining its role as the directory where systems publish available services and consumers discover them.

subclasses.name: System Design Description Sy SDD
subclasses.description: System Design Description Sy SDD is a subclass of AH System Documentation Document providing a detailed internal description of how a software system is designed and built, including its components, architecture, and implementation choices. It complements the external System Description by providing the technical depth needed to develop, deploy, and maintain the system.

subclasses.name: AH Application System Sy SDD
subclasses.description: AH Application System Sy SDD is a subclass of System Design Description Sy SDD providing the detailed, internal design description of an Arrowhead application system, specifying its components, architecture, and implementation choices to support the development, deployment, and maintenance of that specific application system.

subclasses.name: AH Core System Sy SDD
subclasses.description: AH Core System Sy SDD is a subclass of System Design Description Sy SDD providing the detailed, internal design description of an Arrowhead core system, applicable to both mandatory and automation supporting core systems, specifying their internal structure and implementation choices needed to build and maintain those systems.

subclasses.name: AH Automation Supporting System Sy SDD
subclasses.description: AH Automation Supporting System Sy SDD is a subclass of AH Core System Sy SDD providing the detailed, internal design description of an Arrowhead automation supporting system, an optional core system that extends the mandatory infrastructure, specifying its internal architecture and the implementation choices needed to build and deploy it.

subclasses.name: AH Device Registry System Sy SDD
subclasses.description: AH Device Registry System Sy SDD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting System Sy SDD providing the detailed, internal design description of the Device Registry System, specifying how it is built to maintain and manage a registry of physical hardware devices within an Arrowhead environment.

subclasses.name: AH Gatekeeper System Sy SDD
subclasses.description: AH Gatekeeper System Sy SDD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting System Sy SDD providing the detailed, internal design description of the Gatekeeper System, specifying how it is built to manage the negotiation and authorisation of inter-cloud service exchanges between separate Arrowhead local environments.

subclasses.name: AH Gateway System Sy SDD
subclasses.description: AH Gateway System Sy SDD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting System Sy SDD providing the detailed, internal design description of the Gateway System, specifying how it is built to relay data across the boundary between separate Arrowhead local environments once inter-cloud access has been established.

subclasses.name: AH Historian Sy SDD
subclasses.description: AH Historian Sy SDD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting System Sy SDD providing the detailed, internal design description of the Historian system, specifying how it is built to record, store, and provide access to historical operational data from the Arrowhead environment.

subclasses.name: AH QoS Manager Sy SDD
subclasses.description: AH QoS Manager Sy SDD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting System Sy SDD providing the detailed, internal design description of the Quality of Service Manager system, specifying how it is built to monitor and enforce performance and reliability characteristics of service exchanges within the local environment.

subclasses.name: AH System Registry System Sy SDD
subclasses.description: AH System Registry System Sy SDD is a subclass of AH Automation Supporting System Sy SDD providing the detailed, internal design description of the System Registry system, specifying how it is built to catalogue and manage information about the software systems active within an Arrowhead environment.

subclasses.name: AH Mandatory Core System Sy SDD
subclasses.description: AH Mandatory Core System Sy SDD is a subclass of AH Core System Sy SDD providing the detailed, internal design description of one of the three mandatory core systems required in every Arrowhead local environment, specifying the internal architecture and implementation choices for the Service Registry, Orchestrator, or Authorization system.

subclasses.name: AH Authorization System Sy SDD
subclasses.description: AH Authorization System Sy SDD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core System Sy SDD providing the detailed, internal design description of the Authorization System, specifying how it is built to implement authentication and access control for service exchanges within an Arrowhead local environment.

subclasses.name: AH Orchestration System Sy SDD
subclasses.description: AH Orchestration System Sy SDD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core System Sy SDD providing the detailed, internal design description of the Orchestration System, specifying how it is built to match service consumer requests to appropriate service providers at runtime within an Arrowhead local environment.

subclasses.name: AH Service Registry System Sy SDD
subclasses.description: AH Service Registry System Sy SDD is a subclass of AH Mandatory Core System Sy SDD providing the detailed, internal design description of the Service Registry System, specifying how it is built to implement the service publication and discovery directory function in every Arrowhead local environment.

subclasses.name: System Web Application Description WADL
subclasses.description:
Description of an Arrowhead compliant software system in terms of the Web Application Description Language WADL.
The Web Application Description Language (WADL) is a machine-readable XML description of HTTP-based web services. WADL models the resources provided by a service and the relationships between them. WADL is intended to simplify the reuse of web services that are based on the existing HTTP architecture of the Web. It is platform and language independent and aims to promote reuse of applications beyond the basic use in a web browser.
WADL is the REST equivalent of SOAP's Web Services Description Language (WSDL), which can also be used to describe REST web services. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_Application_Description_Language
Sun Microsystems (31 August 2009). "Web Application Description Language: W3C Member Submission 31 August 2009". World Wide Web Consortium. Retrieved 12 August 2012.
World Wide Web Consortium (14 October 2009). "Team Comment on the "Web Application Description Language" Submission". World Wide Web Consortium. Retrieved 12 August 2012.
Lawrence Mandel (29 May 2008). "Describe REST Web services with WSDL 2.0: A how-to guide". IBM. Retrieved 12 August 2012.

subclasses.name: AH Authorization System WADL
subclasses.description: AH Authorization System WADL is a subclass of System Web Application Description WADL representing the machine-readable XML description of the Authorization System's HTTP-based web service interface, formally specifying the resources and operations it exposes to support automated client integration and tool-generated documentation.

subclasses.name: AH Orchestrator WADL
subclasses.description: AH Orchestrator WADL is a subclass of System Web Application Description WADL representing the machine-readable XML description of the Orchestration System's HTTP-based web service interface, formally specifying the resources and operations it exposes for service matching and consumer-provider coordination.

subclasses.name: AH Service Registry WADL
subclasses.description: AH Service Registry WADL is a subclass of System Web Application Description WADL representing the machine-readable XML description of the Service Registry System's HTTP-based web service interface, formally specifying the resources and operations it exposes for service registration and discovery.

subclasses.name: AH System Of Systems Documentation Document
subclasses.description: AH System Of Systems Documentation Document is a subclass of Documentation Document representing any formal document produced as part of the documentation of a system of systems within the Arrowhead Framework. These documents describe composed, multi-system deployments at the level of the overall architecture, covering both collective purpose and internal composition design.

subclasses.name: System Of Systems Description So SD
subclasses.description: System Of Systems Description So SD is a subclass of AH System Of Systems Documentation Document providing a plain, external description of a composed system of systems, explaining which systems participate, what collective capability emerges from their interaction, and the role of the composition in the overall automation solution, without specifying internal design details.

subclasses.name: System Of Systems Design Description So SDD
subclasses.description: System Of Systems Design Description So SDD is a subclass of AH System Of Systems Documentation Document providing a detailed, internal description of how a system of systems is architected and composed, specifying inter-system dependencies, orchestration decisions, and the technical choices that govern how constituent systems work together to realise the intended automation capability.

subclasses.name: Information Model
subclasses.description: An information model in software engineering is a representation of concepts and the relationships, constraints, rules, and operations to specify data semantics for a chosen domain of discourse. Typically it specifies relations between kinds of things, but may also include relations with individual things.

subclasses.name: Local Network
subclasses.description: A local area network is a computer network that interconnects computers within a limited area

subclasses.name: Method
subclasses.description: Method of a service: method that is provided by a service within a SoA.

subclasses.name: Service
subclasses.description:
In the context of the Arrowhead Framework a Service is the information exchanged from a providing system to a consuming system.
• is based on a number of service orientation principles derived from high level objectives and properties of the Arrowhead framework
• can be realized by an arbitrary number of service producers and service consumers
• a system can consume a number of services, process and provide other services to fulfil a more complex task
• can only be provided by technical systems
• can support operational activities within business processes
• can support non-functional requirements, such as real-time
• can have stakeholders, with an interest in business benefit, in one or more specific area of interest
• can have an appointed stakeholder, responsible for the governance of the Service (definition, development).
(Source: Arrowhead Framework Definitions V2.4 & Arrowhead Device Registry Presentation)

subclasses.name: AH Service
subclasses.description: AH Service is a subclass of Service representing a service deployed and governed within the Eclipse Arrowhead Framework, adhering to its principles of loose coupling and late runtime binding. Each AH Service is documented through a Service Description and one or more Interface Design Descriptions, and is classified as either a core service supporting framework operation or an application service addressing a specific use case.

subclasses.name: AH Application Service
subclasses.description: Application services – they are application specific and are implemented by application systems along with functionalities (to match requirements of an application)

subclasses.name: AH Core Service
subclasses.description: AH Core Service is a subclass of AH Service representing the built-in services provided by the Arrowhead Framework's own core systems rather than by application-specific systems. Core services are divided into mandatory core services, which must be present in every local cloud, and automation supporting services, which are optional extensions providing additional operational capabilities.

subclasses.name: AH Automation Supporting Service
subclasses.description: AH Automation Supporting Service is a subclass of AH Core Service representing an optional, built-in service that extends the Arrowhead Framework beyond its three mandatory core services. Unlike the mandatory core services, automation supporting services are not required for a local cloud to function but enrich its operational scope with additional capabilities such as event handling, data management, session control, inter-cloud communication, device and system discovery, or quality-of-service monitoring.

subclasses.name: AH Mandatory Core Service
subclasses.description: AH Mandatory Core Service is a subclass of AH Core Service representing the three services that must be present in every Arrowhead local environment: the service directory enabling systems to find one another, the access control service governing which systems may communicate, and the coordination service matching consumers to appropriate providers. Without these three services, a local cloud cannot operate.

subclasses.name: Service Documentation
subclasses.description: Service documentation is any communicable material that is used to describe, explain or instruct regarding some attributes of a service

subclasses.name: AH Service Documentation
subclasses.description: AH Service Documentation is a subclass of Service Documentation representing the complete documentation set for a service within the Arrowhead Framework, comprising at minimum a Service Description and an Interface Design Description, and optionally a Communication Profile and Semantic Profile. Together these documents specify both the purpose and the technical implementation of the service in a standardised and reusable form.

subclasses.name: Service Oriented Architecture
subclasses.description: Service-oriented architecture (SoA) is a style of software design where services are provided to the other components by application components, through a communication protocol over a network.

subclasses.name: Arrowhead
subclasses.description: Arrowhead is a subclass of Service Oriented Architecture representing the Eclipse Arrowhead Framework, an industrial automation and IoT implementation of service-oriented architecture principles. It organises software systems and services within local clouds, enforcing service registration, access control, and runtime orchestration through mandatory core systems, and enabling flexible, interoperable composition of automation system of systems.

object_properties.name: is implemented by serivce oriented architecture implementation

subclasses.name: SoA Property
subclasses.description: SoA Property is a class representing a quality or characteristic of a service-oriented architecture, such as loose coupling, late binding, discoverability, or interoperability, that governs how the architecture and its services are designed and expected to behave. Within the Arrowhead Framework, SoA properties guide compliance verification and design decisions at both service and system level.

subclasses.name: Software System
subclasses.description: System software is software designed to provide a platform for other software.

subclasses.name: AH System
subclasses.description: AH System is a subclass of Software System representing any software system that is compliant with and deployed within the Eclipse Arrowhead Framework. An AH System participates in the framework by providing and consuming services through the core systems, and is classified as either a core system providing built-in framework infrastructure or an application system addressing a specific use case.

subclasses.name: AH Application System
subclasses.description: AH Application System is a subclass of AH System representing a software system built to address a specific, real-world automation or IoT use case rather than to provide Arrowhead Framework infrastructure. Application systems interact with the framework by registering, discovering, and exchanging services through the core systems, and are disjoint from core systems.

subclasses.name: AH Core System
subclasses.description:
Software system, that belongs to the "standard" components offered by Arrowhead framework.
Arrowhead core systems can occur once in each Arrowhead Local Cloud.
Arriwhead Core Systems can be distinguished in Arrowhead Mandatory Core Systems and Automation supporting systems. Mandatory core systems must exist in each Arrowhead Local Cloud, Automation supporting systems can occur in an Arrowhead Local Cloud.

subclasses.name: AH Automation Supporting System
subclasses.description: AH Automation Supporting System is a subclass of AH Core System representing an optional, built-in system that extends the mandatory core infrastructure of an Arrowhead local cloud with additional capabilities such as device registration, event handling, data management, inter-cloud communication, or quality-of-service monitoring. Unlike mandatory core systems, automation supporting systems are not required for a local cloud to function but enrich its operational scope.

subclasses.name: AH Mandatory Core System
subclasses.description: AH Mandatory Core System is a subclass of AH Core System representing one of the three systems that must be present in every Arrowhead local environment: the Service Registry that enables systems to publish and discover services, the Orchestrator that dynamically matches consumers to appropriate service providers, and the Authorization system that enforces access control between communicating systems.

subclasses.name: System Documentation
subclasses.description: System documentation is any communicable material that is used to describe, explain or instruct regarding some attributes of a system

subclasses.name: AH System Documentation
subclasses.description: AH System Documentation is a subclass of System Documentation representing the complete documentation set for an individual system within the Arrowhead Framework, covering both the external System Description that explains the system's purpose and services, and the internal System Design Description that specifies how it is built, together providing the information needed to understand, implement, and integrate the system.

subclasses.name: AH System Of Systems Documentation
subclasses.description: AH System Of Systems Documentation is a subclass of System Documentation representing the complete documentation set for a composed system of systems within the Arrowhead Framework, covering both the overall description of the composition and its internal design, providing the information needed to engineer, deploy, and validate multi-system Arrowhead automation solutions.

subclasses.name: System Of Systems
subclasses.description: System of systems is a collection of task-oriented or dedicated systems that pool their resources and capabilities together to create a new, more complex system which offers more functionality and performance than simply the sum of the constituent systems.

name: Organization Lobe
description: The Organization Lobe refers to the structural and managerial aspects such as organizational structure, roles and responsibilities, efficient coordination and collaboration among various stakeholders within the semiconductor supply chains.

subclasses.name: Geographical Location
subclasses.description: Name of country or region

subclasses.name: Role
subclasses.description: Business Role (Person) that performs task. Object to describe the role. Type of responsibility is defined by the linkage between function or activity and role. Options: carries out, contributes, must be informed.

subclasses.name: Project Manager
subclasses.description: Project managers have the responsibility of the planning, procurement and execution of a project, in any undertaking that has a defined scope, defined start and a defined finish; regardless of industry.

subclasses.name: Project Owner
subclasses.description: Defines BP for target achievement.

subclasses.name: Project Team Member
subclasses.description: Project team members are the individuals who actively work on one or more phases of the project.

subclasses.name: Agent
subclasses.description:
"The Agent class is the class of agents; things that do stuff. A well known sub-class is Person, representing people. Other kinds of agents include Organization and Group.

The Agent class is useful in a few places in FOAF where Person would have been overly specific. For example, the IM chat ID properties such as jabberID are typically associated with people, but sometimes belong to software bots."

subclasses.name: Person
subclasses.description: The Person class represents people. Something is a Person if it is a person. We don't nitpic about whether they're alive, dead, real, or imaginary. The Person class is a sub-class of the Agent class, since all people are considered 'agents' in FOAF.

subclasses.name: Organization
subclasses.description: Represents a collection of people organized together into a community or other social, commercial or political structure. The group has some common purpose or reason for existence which goes beyond the set of people belonging to it and can act as an Agent. Organizations are often decomposed into hierarchical structures.

subclasses.name: Organizational Unit
subclasses.description: An Organization such as a department or support unit which is part of some larger Organization and only has full recognition within the context of that Organization. In particular the unit would not be regarded as a legal entity in its own right.

subclasses.name: Division
subclasses.description: A division is a administrative business unit that is smaller than the whole company, but it is self-contained and most often responsible for its own revenue, cost, and profit. It has one or more business lines.

subclasses.name: Product Line
subclasses.description: A product line is an organizational unit that can be assigned to a business line and directly owns/is responsible for products.

object_properties.name: is sub unit of business line
responsible for application area product line

subclasses.name: Business Line
subclasses.description: A business line is an organizational unit that can be assigned to a division and can have one or more product lines.

subclasses.name: Category
subclasses.description: Categorizes the project in a big, medium or small project. Usually according the project size.

subclasses.name: Central Function
subclasses.description: Large companies have central fuctions like the Finance or corporate suppyl chain department.

subclasses.name: Certification
subclasses.description: An official document, as proof that something has happened or been done

subclasses.name: Project
subclasses.description: Achievement of the project objective requires these deliverables to conform to specific requirements, including multiple constraints such as time, cost, resources and quality standards or requirements.

subclasses.name: Company Project
subclasses.description: Projects that are or have been developed using our methodology, based on the IPMA standard.

subclasses.name: Project Status
subclasses.description: The current status of the project

subclasses.name: Region
subclasses.description: Large companies divide their activites in regions, like in America, Greater China, SEA (South East Asia), Europe and ROW (rest of World).

subclasses.name: Sub Project
subclasses.description: A project within a larger project.

subclasses.name: Training
subclasses.description: The process of learning the skills you need to do a particular job or activity

subclasses.name: Work Package
subclasses.description: A work package is a group of related tasks within a project.

subclasses.name: Organization
subclasses.description: An organization is en entity comprising multiple people. In SSC, this class mainly refers to businesses.

subclasses.name: Capacity
subclasses.description: CAPACITY with respect to the Domain Semiconductor and Supply Chains Containing Semiconductor is the maximum number of products or a group of products a machine or a group of machines can produce. As soon as a machine has free capacity: 1. all lots which belongs to a priority class have to be dispatched immediately according to their priority rank.

subclasses.name: Required Capacity
subclasses.description: The amount of production capability, such as machinery, that is needed at specific points in the supply chain to fulfill the anticipated demand for semiconductor products within a given timeframe.

subclasses.name: Available Capacity
subclasses.description: The AVAILABLE CAPACITY describes the ability of a resource within a period of time to perform activities or processes. Elmaghraby (2011) refers to this as operational capacity, i.e. the productive capacity that is obtained from the nominal capacity by subtracting the anticipated and unavoidable loss in productivity, for instance, due to machine breakdowns in a wafer fab.

subclasses.name: Capacity Bottleneck
subclasses.description: A CAPACITY BOTTLENECK describes a machine or another element, which constrains the flow of a product. The throughput of the Capacity Bottlenecks define the throughput of a production line.

subclasses.name: Plan
subclasses.description: A PLAN is an activity specification with an intended purpose.

subclasses.name: Allocation Plan
subclasses.description: An allocation plan is a special plan, which deals with assigning ATP quantities to a customer or a customer class.

subclasses.name: Master Plan
subclasses.description: A master plan is a specific plan which determines which quantity resulting from confirmed orders and from forecasted demand should be completed in which location in which period of the planning horizon. Moreover, outsourcing decisions have to be represented in master plans.

subclasses.name: Order Delivery Plan
subclasses.description: This is the result of the order promise or repromise process for different sets of orders taking into account an allocation policy and the supply and allocation situation. Different order promising variants can be distinguished, for instance online order promising, batch order promising, and hybrid order promising. The same is true of repromising.

subclasses.name: Online Order Promising Plan
subclasses.description: Online Order Promising Plan is a dynamic, real-time planning process that evaluates incoming customer orders against current supply chain data—such as inventory availability, production capacity, and supply constraints—to generate immediate and reliable delivery commitments. This plan balances customer demand with supply chain capabilities, ensuring optimized resource utilization and meeting order fulfillment timelines.

subclasses.name: Order Repromising Plan
subclasses.description: Orde Repromising Plan is the (daily) updated or confirmation plan based on (daily) updated ATP and (daily) updated orders

subclasses.name: Planning Purpose
subclasses.description: The PLANNING PURPOSE specifies the objectives of a certain planning activity. It is given by a set of performance measures that are related to a set of PLANNING OBJECTS.

subclasses.name: Criteria
subclasses.description: Typical CRITERIA are maximization, minimization, i.e. if an optimization problem is considered, or larger or smaller than a prescribed value of the certain performance measure, a so-called target, i.e. if a satisfaction problem is solved. In a multi-criteria setting, the dominance concept for plans is of interest.

subclasses.name: Decision Maker Type
subclasses.description: We distinguish human decision-makers (human DECISION-MAKING UNITS) from fully automated DECISION-MAKING UNITS where computers make fully automated decisions. Between these two extremes there are semi-automated decisions, where a computer provides several decision alternatives and a human decision-maker chooses among them. Note that the decision-maker type can change over time.

subclasses.name: Automated
subclasses.description: The entities, processes, or systems designed to function autonomously within a defined scope of the semiconductor supply chain.

subclasses.name: Human
subclasses.description: Human - the decision-making agents that contribute to strategic planning, operational controls, problem-solving, and the execution of tasks across the supply chain lifecycle.

subclasses.name: Semi Automated
subclasses.description: Between these two extremes there are semi-automated decisions, where a computer provides several decision alternatives and a human decision-maker chooses among them.

subclasses.name: Decision Making Initiative
subclasses.description: We distinguish fully autonomous DECISION-MAKING UNITS from DECISION-MAKING UNITS where the decision-making activities are triggered by other DECISION-MAKING UNITS. Note that the decision-making initiative can change over time in a situation-dependent manner.

subclasses.name: Autonomous
subclasses.description: A self-governing or self-directed capability within a structured system that enables independent decision-making and action without requiring external human intervention.

subclasses.name: Dependent
subclasses.description: A subordinate decision-making initiative, where the decision or action relies on the outcome, approval, or input from another independent or external element. In this hierarchical structure, the dependent initiative lacks autonomy and reacts or adapts based on a superior or precursor initiative's information, timing, or directives.

subclasses.name: Decision Making Unit
subclasses.description: The DECISION-MAKING UNIT specifies an instance that makes decisions.

subclasses.name: Decision Making Unit Character
subclasses.description: In an ANTAGO¬NISTIC SETTING, the different DECISION-MAKING UNITS try to meet their own objectives which are in conflict. In a non-antagonistic setting, the DECISION-MAKING UNITS do not exploit their private knowledge in an opportunistic way.

subclasses.name: Edge
subclasses.description: EDGE in the supply chain refers to the use of edge computing technologies to process data closer to where it is generated—such as warehouses, factories, vehicles or others —rather than relying on centralized cloud systems. By enabling real-time data analysis and decision-making at the "edge" of the network, companies can reduce latency, enhance operational responsiveness, and improve visibility across the supply chain.

subclasses.name: Frozen Fence
subclasses.description: FROZEN FENCE is used to set a frozen interval in which decision making is not allowed, or a defined exception, to change the previously determined values.

subclasses.name: Hierarchical Situation
subclasses.description: HIERARCHICAL SITUATION refers to the structured, multi-level arrangement of entities, processes, or decision-making authority within the supply chain. It outlines e.g. how different layers—such as suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, and retailers—interact based on levels of control, responsibility, and information flow.

subclasses.name: Distributed Hierarchical Situation
subclasses.description: In this situation, edges referring to instructions and reactions are possible.

subclasses.name: Heterarchical Situation
subclasses.description: Heterarchical Situation is a type of hierarchical situation where all entities, represented as vertices within a structure, exist on the same hierarchical level (level 1). It describes a balanced, non-rank-based relationship among entities in a system, such that no entity dominates or is subordinate to another.

subclasses.name: Strict Hierarchical Situation
subclasses.description: Strict Hierarchical Situation is a structured scenario, organisational framework, or system state within the semiconductor supply chain in which all entities, processes, or decisions follow a rigid hierarchy characterised by clear, predefined levels of authority, responsibility, or dependency. In such situations, relationships between entities, such as resources, processes, operations, or managerial roles, are strictly governed by vertical or layered structures, where lower level elements depend on or are constrained by higher level elements.

subclasses.name: Performance Measure
subclasses.description: PERFORMANCE MEASURE is defined by a calculation procedure. Performance measures can be blended using weights to express the importance of the different measures.

subclasses.name: Plan Execution
subclasses.description: A PLAN EXECUTION is related to performing the activities according to a PLAN either directly in the base system, for instance, releasing lots into a wafer fab, or as instructions for another DECISION-MAKING UNIT.

subclasses.name: Planning Approach
subclasses.description: PLANNING APPROACH is a specific planning algorithm which is used in a deticated planning process.

subclasses.name: Planning Constraint
subclasses.description:
In the planning domain a PLANNING CONSTRAINTS is often referred to capacity limitation, which limit the quantities that can be produced on an equipment or a fab for a certain product or product groups. Other Constraints can be workforce or material. Constraints can be temporary and can change. 
Most popular academic definition: A PLANNING CONSTRAINT restricts the action space. This space is formed by alternative actions that are a result of the planning decisions (Schneeweis 2003).

subclasses.name: Resource Availability Constraints
subclasses.description: This type of constraints has an impact on the assignment of activities to RESOURCES and to START/END TIMES to ACTIVITIES.

subclasses.name: Resource Compatibility Constraints
subclasses.description: This type of constraints ensures that only allowed activities are performed using a given RESOURCE.

subclasses.name: Temporal Constraints
subclasses.description: The time-based restrictions, limitations, or conditions that govern or influence the scheduling, sequencing, synchronization, or completion of processes, tasks, or resource allocations within the semiconductor supply chain.

subclasses.name: Planning Decision
subclasses.description: The PLANNING DECISIONS is the best choice out of options, determined by the DECISION-MAKING UNIT.

subclasses.name: Planning Function
subclasses.description: PLANNING FUNCTION describes the different functions and its properies follwing the supply chain planning matrix.

subclasses.name: Planning Instance
subclasses.description: A PLANNING INSTANCE specifies the PLANNING OBJECTS and the values of related PLANNING CONSTRAINTS that form the basis for a planning decision.

subclasses.name: Planning Object
subclasses.description: A PLANNING OBJECT specifies what has to be planned as an atomic unit. A single PLANNING OBJECT typically represents a quantity of a certain product or product aggregate to be released or completed within a certain period in a certain node of the semiconductor supply chain. Other PLANNING OBJECTS can be orders or lots. Values are assigned to the attributes of a PLANNING OBJECT as a result of a planning decision.

subclasses.name: Planning Process
subclasses.description: The PLANNING PROCESS specifies under which circumstances which (re)planning activities are performed by a DECISION-MAKING UNIT.

subclasses.name: Planning Situation
subclasses.description: The PLANNING SITUATION describes the organization of several DECISION-MAKING UNITS and also its environment.

subclasses.name: Process
subclasses.description: A PROCESS is a collection of subprocesses that meet a specific business objective. E.g. Perform Sourcing or Purchase Materials and Services. A production PROCESS specifies a method of making a product at a location. The process is expressed at a coarse level of granularity suitable for use in production planning.

subclasses.name: Product Aggregate
subclasses.description: A PRODUCT AGGREGATE combines individual products into a product group, called a PRODUCT AGGREGATE. This results in a reduction of complexity, which enables a better overview.

subclasses.name: Product Hierarchy
subclasses.description: A PRODUCT HIERARCHY characterizes the top-down and bottom-up relationship between different product aggregates. It organizes the product aggregates according to defined criteria. A product aggregate is used to group different products based on certain criteria. The grouping criteria depends often on the planning purpose (e.g. controlling, production). It is a certain view on a set of products.

subclasses.name: Replanning Degree
subclasses.description: REPLANNING DEGREE is the degree of change between an updated plan and a previous plan.

subclasses.name: Target
subclasses.description: TARGETS are prescribed values for the different performance measures.

subclasses.name: Vertex
subclasses.description: VERTEX plays a crucial role in the financial and compliance side of the supply chain. Its solutions help businesses calculate, manage, and report indirect taxes (like sales tax, VAT, and GST) at the relevant point in the supply chain, from procurement to distribution.

subclasses.name: Planning
subclasses.description: PLANNING is an activity with the purpose to determine a plan. Planning is associated with goals, represented by objective functions to be optimized.

subclasses.name: Allocation Planning
subclasses.description: The process of distributing ATP (available to promise) to region or a customer group or a customer.

subclasses.name: Master Planning
subclasses.description: Master Planning is the overarching, strategic process of balancing supply, demand, and capacity at a global level to ensure the optimized planning and execution of semiconductor supply chain operations. It involves the alignment of production schedules, inventory levels, and resource allocation across all stages of the supply chain—from wafer fabrication and assembly/testing to distribution—with the goal of meeting customer demands, minimizing costs, and maximizing efficiency.

subclasses.name: Order Promising
subclasses.description: This concept describes the process to promise an order considering allocation policy as well as supply and allocation situation. The order promising can be distinguished between different variants, for instance online order promising and batch order promising.

subclasses.name: Aggregated Capacity
subclasses.description: The AGGREGATED CAPACITY GROUP (ACG) combines products that are interchangeable in production resources (e.g. can be produced on the same equipment) and having the same capacity consumption. Using an ACG provides flexibility in a way of switching demands of this products within this ACG.

subclasses.name: Resource Capacity
subclasses.description: Resource capacity planning is about comparing future resource utilization of project resources against available capacity to do work.

subclasses.name: Bottleneck Resource
subclasses.description: A bottleneck resource is an obstacle to smooth flow in a process.

subclasses.name: Allocated Available To Promise
subclasses.description: The AATP (Allocated Available To Promise) is this part of the ATP (Available To Promise) which is already located to a certain customer(group) or a region.

subclasses.name: Available To Promise
subclasses.description: The ATP (Available to promise) is todays and upcoming Availability of products for demand fulfillment and order promising.

subclasses.name: Confirmation
subclasses.description: A CONFIRMATION is an order acknowledgement with a due date from the supplier.

subclasses.name: Customer Logistics Management Representative
subclasses.description: A CUSTOMER LOGISTICS MANAGEMENT REPRESENTATIVE (CLM) is a typical name for one “face” to the customer, taking care of all customers supply chain topics. He/she is responsible for the demand fulfilment process – Usage of ATP. It is his/her task to ensure in-time delivery to customers based on orders and forecasts. He/she is usually also taking care of forecast in a midterm time horizon (typical for that is the EDI FORECAST)

subclasses.name: General Customer
subclasses.description: No description yet

subclasses.name: Marketing Demand
subclasses.description: MARKETING DEMAND is a supply chain or production request for a specific product, product group or service, coming from the market. Either demand exists explicitly in form of customer need (e.g. orders or EDI forecast) or implicitly as expected customer need.

subclasses.name: NEWs
subclasses.description: A nEW is a negative Early Warning and it means that a new customer order confirmation is worse (later order confirmation date) than the previous order confirmation. nEWs is the plural of nEW.

subclasses.name: Open Order Book
subclasses.description: An OPEN ORDER BOOK is a business's list of open, unshipped, customer orders, normally time-phased and valued at actual individual order prices, that may include margin and profitability analysis.

subclasses.name: Operational Demand
subclasses.description: OPERATIONAL DEMAND is a supply chain or production request for a specific product, product group or service, coming from company intern business division. Either demand exists explicitly in form of customer need (e.g. orders or EDI forecast) or implicitly as expected customer need.OPERATIONAL DEMAND is a supply chain or production request for a specific product, product group or service, coming from company intern business division. Either demand exists explicitly in form of customer need (e.g. orders or EDI forecast) or implicitly as expected customer need.

subclasses.name: Forecast
subclasses.description: Forecast is an unconstrained prospect about the customer future demand.

subclasses.name: AP FCST
subclasses.description: Allocation Priority Forecast. To be used in case of too high order picture on special products. The system should usually consider the amount of the entered run rates only. AP_FCST is usually the highest priority in capacity planning.

subclasses.name: HP Forecast
subclasses.description: High Priority Forecast is an implicitly expected, internally generated demand signal of the highest priority. It is used in supply chain planning under constrained supply conditions to strategically reserve and protect generated supply ahead of order confirmation. Demand planned from HP_FCST is not allocated to specific customer orders automatically, but is held for strategic distribution decisions, such as serving preferred customers or fulfilling high value demand. As a subclass of Operational_Demand, it represents an implicit expected customer need, originating from an internal business division rather than a direct customer order.

subclasses.name: NP Forecast
subclasses.description: Normal Priority Forecast. To be used for quantity reservation that orders from other products can consume. To be used if not clear if an order might come. Orders from other products can push these booked quantities and use this capacity just in time. Priority is lower than an order; a mix with other forecasts is possible.

subclasses.name: OP Forecast
subclasses.description: Order Priority Forecast. To be used for quantity reservations that should not be consumed by orders of other products, for example earlier entering. Orders from other products cannot consume into this booked quantity of capacity. Priority is higher than an order; a mix with other forecasts is possible.

subclasses.name: SSO Stocks
subclasses.description: SSO Stocks refers to SSO stock profiles applied exclusively at the finished goods level, sourced from Stockplan Rules or manually entered in the SPL UI. This class encompasses three subtypes: Retained Stock, which is handled together with AP_FCST settings via retain stock rules; Min Stock, representing the minimum inventory level desired on hand to buffer small capacity problems; and Max Stock, representing the maximum inventory level permitted, used to fill capacities.

subclasses.name: Max Stock
subclasses.description: The amount of inventory which should not be exceeded. The limit is normally determined after considering storage space of the facilities, how quickly inventory is sold or used, cost of insurance on inventory, and the risk of inventory becoming outdated before it is used.

subclasses.name: Min Stock
subclasses.description: The minimum level of inventory is a kind of a precautionary level of inventory which indicates that the delivery of raw materials or merchandise may take more than the normal lead time.

subclasses.name: Ramp Up Stock
subclasses.description: Ramp Up Stock is a subclass of inventory stock targets used in supply chain planning to build up a buffer of finished goods or intermediate components ahead of a new product launch. It is applied in situations where customer orders have not yet entered the system, but the supply planning team wants physical inventory pre positioned and available in anticipation of future demand. As part of the broader family of stock targets, it functions as a proactive, forward looking inventory measure, distinct from safety or maximum stock targets, specifically designed to support the early stage ramp of new products and ensure supply readiness before commercial demand materializes.

subclasses.name: Retained Stock
subclasses.description: Retained Stock is a subclass of SSO Stocks representing an operational inventory buffer held at a distribution center to absorb unplanned supply fluctuations, such as short term demand increases or unexpectedly low inbound deliveries. As part of the broader SSO Stocks family, which governs strategic stock profiles at the finished goods level, Retained Stock works by temporarily hiding a portion of the available on hand inventory from the active demand supply matching process. This ensures that planned production or replenishment targets are pursued regardless of the current buffer level, preserving supply continuity without requiring manual intervention in the planning cycle.

subclasses.name: Safety Stock
subclasses.description: Describes a level of extra stock that is maintained to mitigate risk of stockouts  caused by uncertainties in supply and demand.

subclasses.name: Order Line Item
subclasses.description: ORDER LINE ITEM is every product on the order is referenced by a record that includes quantity and usually a customer delivery wish date, as well as a reference to which order it belongs.

subclasses.name: Order Reschedule
subclasses.description: ORDER RESCHEDULE is any change in the requested order delivery date or volume in an order line is referred to as an order rescheduling.

subclasses.name: Order Schedule Line
subclasses.description: ORDER SCHEDULE LINE contains all the delivery related information.

subclasses.name: Prioritized Demand
subclasses.description: The PRIORITIZED DEMAND is the demand that should be covered first.

subclasses.name: Prioritized Orders
subclasses.description: PRIORITIZED ORDERS are Orders that should be completed first.

subclasses.name: Promise
subclasses.description: A PROMISE is the committed portion of supply by the master production schedule and material plan.

subclasses.name: Sales Demand
subclasses.description: A SALES DEMAND is a request for a specific product or service that can have different triggers. Either demand exists explicitly in form of customer orders or implicitly as expected customer need that have to be fulfilled by the semiconductor supply chain.

subclasses.name: Supply Demand Match
subclasses.description: Supply and demand match when sufficient materials exist to cover material demand while taking available capacity into account.

subclasses.name: Supply Picture
subclasses.description: A SUPPLY PICTURE is a visualization of the supply in its dimensions. Supply is the total amount of specific products that is available to customers. Supply has the dimensions quantity, time, location, product, including aggregation of all dimensions. Supply is defined as inventory or plan replenishment.

subclasses.name: Target Allocation
subclasses.description: The TARGET ALLOCATION is the level of allocation planned by the company.

name: Power Lobe
description:
Power refers to the electrical energy consumed or dissipated by electronic devices or components during their operation, and is a crucial consideration for efficiency and performance optimization.

The Power lobe models the Amplication Switching Device, Control Method, Device Configuration and Element, Document, Entity, and Gate Driver.
It also represents the notions of Industrial Sector, Information Object, Operation Mode, Process, Process Input and Output.
It maps the topics of Product, Resistance, SiC MOSFET, switcher, and Voltage.

subclasses.name: Control Method
subclasses.description: It is the method used to turn on, turn off , increaseing, and decreasing output current/voltage.

subclasses.name: Voltage Controlled
subclasses.description: by applying the voltage between Gate and Sourcet o turn on, turn off the MOSFET, and  increaseing, decreasing  the MOSFET output current.

subclasses.name: Device Configuration
subclasses.description: Device configuration can refer to either hardware or software , or the combination of both.

subclasses.name: N Channel Configuration
subclasses.description: N-Channel Configuration is the hardware and/or software settings for the use of one or more N-channel field effect transistors (N-channel MOSFETs/FETs) within a power circuit. It documents electrical connections and orientation (source, drain, gate), intended role (for example high side switch, load switch, complementary stage), gate drive and level shifting schemes, biasing and pull up elements, gate resistances, protection/snubbing components, allowed voltage/current/thermal limits, switching profiles, and any monitoring or control parameters required for safe and efficient operation. This configuration is used for specification, validation, monitoring and automated control of power assemblies where N-channel devices determine power routing, protection or load isolation.

subclasses.name: P Channel Configuration
