subclasses.description: P_Channel_Configuration - the hardware and/or software settings for the use of one or more P channel field effect transistors (P channel MOSFETs/FETs) within a power circuit. It documents electrical connections and orientation (source, drain, gate), intended role (for example high side switch, load switch, complementary stage), gate drive and level shifting schemes, biasing and pull up elements, gate resistances, protection/snubbing components, allowed voltage/current/thermal limits, switching profiles, and any monitoring or control parameters required for safe and efficient operation. This configuration is used for specification, validation, monitoring and automated control of power assemblies where P channel devices determine power routing, protection or load isolation.

subclasses.name: Device Element
subclasses.description: Elements that are part of a device

subclasses.name: Drain
subclasses.description: Drain - is a Device_Element in the Power_Lobe that represents a component or endpoint that removes, sinks, dissipates, or consumes electrical or energetic power from a system or circuit. Examples include loads, grounding/return points, resistive or mechanical energy absorbers, and heat-dissipating elements. A Drain may be passive or active and can be monitored or controlled; it is used to model power consumption and energy-flow endpoints within the power domain.

subclasses.name: Gate
subclasses.description: Gate - represents a control terminal or component that regulates the flow of electrical current or signals within a power device or circuit. Typical uses include the gate terminal of transistors (which modulates channel conductivity), solid state switching/gating elements, and gate driver interfaces. A Gate is characterized by its control signal (e.g., voltage), switching behaviour, thresholds and timing, and is used for switching, regulation, protection and control of power paths; it can be monitored or driven as part of device or system control.

subclasses.name: Source
subclasses.description: Source - represents a component or endpoint that provides, supplies or generates electrical or energetic power to a circuit, system, or device.

subclasses.name: Entity
subclasses.description: Anything: real, possible, or imaginary, which some modeller wants to talk about for some purpose.

subclasses.name: Abstract
subclasses.description:
Any Entity that cannot be located in space-time.

Example: mathematical entities: formal semantics elements, regions within dimensional spaces, etc."

subclasses.name: Switching Value
subclasses.description:
The value of the result of the method (procedures) of the device function. The result is an information object that encodes some value for a feature. For example:
a) If we consider the observation is the method used for sensing of the sensors, then the observation has a result which is the output of the sensor,
b) If we consider the amplification is the method used for boosting of the power converter, then the amplification has a result which is the output of the  power converter,

subclasses.name: Information Entity
subclasses.description: A piece of information, be it concretely realized or not.

subclasses.name: Information Object
subclasses.description: A piece of information, such as a musical composition, a text, a word, a picture, independently from how it is concretely realized.

subclasses.name: Document
subclasses.description: The document class presents those things which are, broadly conceived, "documents''. It should contain the manuals and the data sheet of the devices.

subclasses.name: Technical Term
subclasses.description: Set up with connection to a function or activity or VAC. It can be either input or output, where the direction of the arrow describes whether it is an input or an output. Set up of a connection is not mandatory.

subclasses.name: Semiconductor Product Data Sheet
subclasses.description: Data sheet of a semiconductor product (its name), SiC MOSFET Data Sheet

subclasses.name: Environmental Data
subclasses.description: Additional information to a process like work schedule, production plans, etc.

subclasses.name: Geometric Dimension
subclasses.description: "Describes the Dimensions of any Physical Object (Length, Wisth, Height)"

subclasses.name: Length

subclasses.description: SiC MOSFET Output, the device output is a piece of information (value), the value itself being represented by an The device function value.

subclasses.name: Object
subclasses.description: Any physical, social, or mental object, or a substance

subclasses.name: Physical Object
subclasses.description: Any physical object

subclasses.name: Interface
subclasses.description: A common boundary or interconnection between systems, equipment, concepts, or human beings

subclasses.name: Package
subclasses.description: A package is the housing for a chip (or several chips) and provides electrical contacts. It is an interconnect in between chip-pads and the interface to the PCB board. A package is characterized by its outline (drawing) and its materials.

subclasses.name: Platform
subclasses.description:
An Entity to which other Entities can be attached - particularly semiconductor products and other platforms.

Example: A post might act as the platform, a body might act as a platform for an attached device.

subclasses.name: System
subclasses.description: System is a unit of abstraction for pieces of infrastructure that implements procedure. A System may have components, its subsystems, which are other systems."

subclasses.name: Social Object
subclasses.description:
Act of carrying out an (Observation) Procedure to estimate or calculate a value of a property of a FeatureOfInterest. Links to an ObservableProperty to describe what the result is an estimate of, and to a FeatureOfInterest to detail what that proeprty was associated with.

Example: The activity of estimating the intensity of an earthquake using the Mercalli intensity scale is an Observation as is measuring the moment magnitude, i.e., the energy released by said earthquake.

subclasses.name: Situation
subclasses.description: A view, consistent with ('satisfying') a Description, on a set of entities. It can also be seen as a 'relational context' created by an observer on the basis of a 'frame' (i.e. a Description). For example, a PlanExecution is a context including some actions executed by agents according to certain parameters and expected tasks to be achieved from a Plan; a DiagnosedSituation is a context of observed entities that is interpreted on the basis of a Diagnosis, etc. Situation is also able to represent reified n-ary relations, where isSettingFor is the top-level relation for all binary projections of the n-ary relation. If used in a transformation pattern for n-ary relations, the designer should take care of creating only one subclass of Situation for each n-ary relation, otherwise the 'identification constraint' (Calvanese et al., IJCAI 2001) could be violated.

subclasses.name: The Method Of The Device Function
subclasses.description:
The function of the devices has a method ( Procedure to estimate or calculate a value), for example:
The Senor its function is the sensing, the sensing method is the observation
The Boost converter ( a type of the power converter) its function is boosting, the boosting method is the amplification.

Act of carrying out an (the method) Procedure to estimate or calculate a value of a property of a FeatureOfInterest. Links to an the methodProperty to describe what the result is an estimate of, and to a FeatureOfInterest to detail what that proeprty was associated with.

Example: The activity of estimating the intensity of an earthquake using the Mercalli intensity scale is an Observation as is measuring the moment magnitude, i.e., the energy released by said earthquake."

subclasses.name: Quality
subclasses.description: Any aspect of an Entity (but not a part of it), which cannot exist without that Entity. For example, the way the surface of a specific PhysicalObject looks like is a Quality, while the encoding of that Quality into e.g. a PhysicalAttribute should be modeled as a Region. From the design viewpoint, the Quality-Region distinction is useful only when individual aspects of an Entity are considered in a domain of discourse. For example, in an automotive context, it would be irrelevant to consider the aspects of car windows for a specific car, unless the factory wants to check a specific window against design parameters (anomaly detection). On the other hand, in an antiques context, the individual aspects for a specific piece of furniture are a major focus of attention, and may constitute the actual added value, because the design parameters for old furniture are often not fixed, and may not be viewed as 'anomalies'.

subclasses.name: Property
subclasses.description: Any attribute of an entity

subclasses.name: Blocking Capability
subclasses.description: Blocking_Capability - is a Property in the Power_Lobe that describes an entity's ability to prevent, stop, or constrain actions, flows, or access in the supply chain (for example: stopping production, rejecting shipments, halting transactions, or restricting access). It covers technical and organizational mechanisms (hard/soft, temporary/conditional) used to enforce such blocks.

subclasses.name: Blocking Voltage
subclasses.description: Blocking_Voltage - is a Property in the Power_Lobe that represents the voltage level at which an electrical device prevents or substantially inhibits current conduction (for example reverse or off state voltage). Values are typically expressed in volts and recorded as numeric measurements with appropriate units.

subclasses.name: Drain Current
subclasses.description: Drain_Current - represents the electrical current drawn, sunk, or consumed by a Drain (power sink or load). It covers instantaneous, steady state, RMS, peak or average current values used to describe, monitor or specify power consumption of a device element. Values are typically expressed in amperes (A) and represented as numeric measurements with associated unit, timestamp and measurement metadata where applicable.

subclasses.name: Drain Source Voltage
subclasses.description: Drain_Source_Voltage - denotes the electrical potential difference between the drain and source terminals of a power device (for example a MOSFET or other transistor), expressed in volts. It characterizes operating conditions (instantaneous or peak) and is used for monitoring, specification, constraint checking and control of power components. Typically represented as a numeric value with unit volts (V).

subclasses.name: Drain Voltage
subclasses.description: Drain_Voltage - representing the electrical potential at a device's drain terminal relative to a reference terminal (typically the source). It denotes the drain-to-source potential difference used to characterize operating and switching behaviour, power flow and device stress; values may be instantaneous, DC, peak or RMS and are expressed in volts (V). This property is used for monitoring, specification, constraint checking and control of power devices.

subclasses.name: Junction Temperature
subclasses.description: The highest operating temperature of the actual semiconductor

subclasses.name: Maximum Junction Temperature
subclasses.description: Is specified in the part's datasheet and is used when calculating the necessary case-to-ambient thermal resistance for a given power dissipation.

subclasses.name: Leakage Current
subclasses.description: Leakage_Current - unintended electric current that flows through or across a device, insulation, or circuit path when the ideal or intended current should be zero. It covers steady state and transient leakage through dielectrics, semiconductors, surface conduction, and insulation breakdown pathways.

subclasses.description: On_State_Power_Loss - the power dissipated by a device or element while it is in its conducting (on) state.

subclasses.description: On_State_Resistance - the electrical resistance of a device when it is in its conducting (on) state.

subclasses.name: On State Voltage
subclasses.description: On_State_Voltage - the electrical voltage associated with a device or circuit element when it is in its conductive ('on') state.

subclasses.name: Operating Property
subclasses.description: A characteristic that describes how a device operates under specified conditions, covering aspects such as power ranges, power sources, standard configurations, or attachments.

subclasses.name: Region Of Operation
subclasses.description: Region_Of_Operation - the permissible or intended multidimensional range(s) of operating conditions for a device, component or system. It is used to capture safe operating areas, nominal/optimal bands, derating limits and constraint boundaries for specification, monitoring, validation and automated control.

subclasses.name: Off State Region
subclasses.description: Off_State_Region - defines the operating conditions under which a device, component, or system is considered ‘off’ or non operational from a power perspective.

subclasses.name: On State Region
subclasses.description: On_State_Region - identifies the set of operating conditions under which a power device or element is considered to be in its ON (conducting) state.

subclasses.name: Triode/Constant Resistance Region
subclasses.description: Triode/Constant_Resistance_Region - is an on state operating region of a semiconductor switching device in which the device conducts with an approximately constant resistance between its terminals.

subclasses.name: Saturation Region
subclasses.description: Saturation_Region - the range of operating conditions in which a power switching device is in its saturation (fully on or active) conduction regime.

subclasses.name: Switching Frequency
subclasses.description: Switching_Frequency - is the rate at which a power-electronic or switching device alternates its state (on/off or between conduction paths), expressed in hertz (Hz). In a supply-chain/topology context it characterizes the temporal switching behavior of converters, inverters, motor drives, relays, and solid-state switches and impacts efficiency, thermal loading, electromagnetic interference (EMI), filter design, component selection, and regulatory compliance.

subclasses.name: Threshold Voltage
subclasses.description: Threshold_Voltage - is the specific electrical potential at which a component or material changes behavior or is considered to have reached an operational or safety limit.

subclasses.name: Gate Driver
subclasses.description: Gate Driver represents a circuit or component that amplifies control signals to switch power semiconductor devices, such as MOSFETs or IGBTs, on and off.

subclasses.name: Industrial Sector
subclasses.description:
The collection of all localized groups of enterprises that are producers of industrial commodities, in which each such group together forms the major industrial sector for the region. 'Industrial commodities' includes MechanicalDevices and basic industrial materials. Examples include 'the world industrial sector', the 'industrial sector of China'. The Chinese water pump industry would not be an exemplar of IndustrialEconomicSector but would rather be a sub-industry (see subIndustries) of it. On the other hand, chinese water pump manufacturers would be considered groupMembers of 'the industrial sector of China'.

This classification is done by The Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS) is an industry taxonomy developed in 1999 by MSCI and Standard & Poor's (S&P) for use by the global financial community. The GICS structure consists of 11 sectors, 24 industry groups, 68 industries and 157 sub-industries[1] into which S&P has categorized all major public companies

subclasses.name: Operation Mode
subclasses.description: Operation_Mode - a defined configuration, behavioral state or control regime of a power-related device, process, or system. It captures the set of operational parameters, control strategies and allowable that determine performance, safety and energy consumption. Operation_Mode is used for specification, monitoring, scheduling and automated control and is linked to Device_Configuration, Control_Method, Process inputs/outputs and Gate_Driver settings to model how components behave in different usage scenarios.

subclasses.name: Depletion Mode
subclasses.description: Depletion_Mode - is an Operation_Mode within the Power_Lobe that characterises system behaviour in which stored energy or power capacity is being reduced due to consumption, discharge or drawdown. It covers cases such as battery discharge, fuel consumption, reserve use or deliberate sustained power draw, and captures relevant properties such as rate of depletion, duration, and effects on availability and performance. Depletion_Mode is used to represent and reason about energy consumption states and transitions of assets, components and systems in the supply chain digital reference model.

subclasses.name: Enhancement Mode
subclasses.description: Enhancement_Mode - represents a configured or temporary operating state intended to increase a device or system's performance, output, responsiveness, or functional capability above its nominal/standard mode. Enhancement_Mode captures the intent, triggers, allowable duration, and associated constraints (such as increased power draw, thermal limits, safety interlocks, and reduced lifetime trade offs) used for monitoring, control, specification and automated transition logic.

For example, a particular Sensor deployed on a Platform, or a whole network of Sensors deployed for an observation campaign. The deployment may have sub processes, such as installation, maintenance, addition, and decomissioning and removal.

The application voltage is used to configure, operate, test, or procure equipment and to ensure compatibility and safety across interconnected components.

name: Process Lobe
description:
Process refers to a series of interconnected and sequential actions, steps, or operations designed to achieve a specific outcome or goal within a system or organization.

The Process lobe of the Digital Reference ontology represents the topics of Agent, Business Process Flow, Function and Function Object.
It also maps the notions of Goal, Input, Model and Model Element, Output, Screen, and Value-added Chain Diagram.

subclasses.name: Goal
subclasses.description: The class Goal represents the desired outcome of a Function

subclasses.name: Activity
subclasses.description: Additional lobes: Time

subclasses.name: Activity
subclasses.description: Activity is a discrete step or unit of work within a modelled process, connected by activity edges to define the process flow.

subclasses.name: Activity Edge
subclasses.description: represents a directed relationship between two Activity nodes in a process model that defines the control, sequence, or information/data dependency governing movement from a source activity to a target activity. It may carry semantics such as sequence flow, conditional guards or triggers, concurrency (fork/join), data/object passage, timing constraints, and responsibility handoffs, and is used to capture dependencies, precedence, coordination, and information transfer in business and supply chain processes.

subclasses.name: Aux Resource Requirement
subclasses.description: A formal specification of the secondary or supporting resources that must be available to indirectly facilitate or enhance the execution of a Process or Function within the semiconductor supply chain, stated as constraints on resource type and capability, quantity/capacity, quality/certification, and temporal availability. These requirements define the conditions under which auxiliary resources — which do not directly transform materials into finished products — must be present to ensure the smooth functioning, quality, reliability, and efficiency of primary resources and processes (e.g., tools, fixtures/jigs, auxiliary equipment, utilities such as compressed air or power, software/IT services, safety gear, calibration devices, and qualified personnel/skills).

subclasses.name: Capability
subclasses.description: Ratio of the theoretical available recipes at a tool and the available recipes

subclasses.name: Kanban
subclasses.description: is a visual, pull based signaling mechanism used to control workflow and material replenishment in production and supply chain processes. Kanban uses cards, bins, boards, electronic tokens, or other signals to represent work items, inventory status, or authorization to produce or move items. By limiting work in progress (WIP) and triggering replenishment only in response to downstream demand, Kanban supports just in time delivery, reduces excess inventory, exposes bottlenecks, and improves flow and responsiveness. Often Kanban replenishment is reach based. In crisis situation a bullwhip accelerator and the user should change to absolute stock replenishment instead of reach based replenishment when the crisis is confirmed.

subclasses.name: Material Consumption
subclasses.description: The quantity and identity of physical materials, components and consumables that a Process withdraws from its inputs and consumes, transforms or incorporates to produce one or more outputs. Material_Consumption records amounts, units and timing, and captures losses, waste, by products and recycled or returned fractions; it links Inputs and Outputs to support planning, costing, traceability, compliance, sustainability and value added chain modeling within the Process lobe.

subclasses.name: Recipe Equipment Config
subclasses.description: represents the explicit configuration of one or more pieces of equipment, their settings, interconnections and operational constraints required to execute a production recipe or recipe step within a process. It captures equipment types and capabilities, control and automation parameters, tooling and sensor mappings, capacities and throughput limits, sequencing/transfer relationships, safety and quality constraints, and version/lifecycle information. In semiconductor manufacturing the SPS (single process step) is often only sufficiently defined with the recipe.

subclasses.name: Business Process Flow
subclasses.description:
An EPC describes a Business Process Flow, which is a sequence of required tasks to create specified outputs using defined inputs.
A Business Process Flow is a sequence of required tasks to create specified outputs using defined inputs.

subclasses.name: Function Object
subclasses.description: In IndustryPrint 5, function objects are used to model the decomposition of a process.

subclasses.name: Modelling Function Object
subclasses.description: Function objects are used to model the decomposition of the process flow.

subclasses.name: Task
subclasses.description: A Task is an instruction of a work package to create the output.

subclasses.name: Process Interface
subclasses.description: Process Interfaces connect several process models on the same Process hierarchical levelby linking the EPCs according to their shared events (also known as "horizontal navigation"). They thus facilitate process structuring and navigation by keeping models concise

subclasses.name: Structural Function Object
subclasses.description: Function objects are used to model the decomposition of the structure of a process.

subclasses.name: Process Group
subclasses.description: A set of a processes covering a single business area. Usually under the ownership of one business process owner and correlates to one module. E.g. Procurement

subclasses.name: Process Type
subclasses.description: A set of core and enabler processes of Infineon on Level 0 (highest level). This level helps helps organizing project work/ development and represents a single track in the oneSAP project. It is based on a Deloitte standard which was adapted to Infineon's needs.

subclasses.name: Subprocess
subclasses.description: A grouping of related tasks that create an output within the larger objective of the subprocess. E.g. Create and Maintain Purchase Orders

subclasses.name: Human Output
subclasses.description: Human being that puts effort in the processing of a process step (function). It belongs to the organizational unit that is responsible for the specific process step.

subclasses.name: Input
subclasses.description: Item external to a system (such as a process) that is transformed by the system (usually together with one or more other items) to become an output.

subclasses.name: Process Service
subclasses.description: Process Service is a subclass of Input representing an externally provided capability or action consumed by a process, being transformed alongside other inputs to contribute to a defined process output or outcome.

subclasses.name: Info Service
subclasses.description: A service whose primary output is information rather than material transformation. It acquires, generates, transforms, stores, retrieves, analyzes, and/or distributes information to support the planning, execution, monitoring, and control of business processes across the value chain. Info_Services may be automated or human-performed and are realized by Functions operating over Information Objects via defined interfaces. Typical resources include IT systems, software applications, data repositories, analytics models, integration platforms, and communication networks; typical constraints include service levels for availability, latency, throughput, accuracy, integrity, confidentiality, and traceability.

subclasses.name: Other Services
subclasses.description: Collection of other services used as input to a production process or which are created during a production process.

subclasses.name: Material
subclasses.description: The matter from which something can be made. Material can include but is not limited to raw and processed material, components, parts, assemblies, sub-assemblies, fuels, lubricants, coolants, cleaning agents, and small tools and accessories that may be consumed directly or indirectly.

subclasses.name: Model
subclasses.description: One striking commonality between EPC meta models is the Process. One process may contain an unlimited number of elements, but a process element is always linked to a specific process. If a process contains an interface, it is always linked to one specific process and represents a refinement of a normal function.

subclasses.name: Process Diagram
subclasses.description: The first level of process decomposition that is comprised of subprocesses that depict a business objective.

subclasses.name: Process Group Map
subclasses.description: A set of a processes covering a single business area. Usually under the ownership of one business process owner and aligning with a function.

subclasses.name: Process Type Map
subclasses.description: A set of process types and related process groups that define the enterprise for a particular industry/sector.

subclasses.name: Subprocess Diagram
subclasses.description: The second and lowest level of process decomposition that is comprised of tasks that depict the role-based activities of the subprocess.

subclasses.name: Model Element
subclasses.description: An EPC model element is part of the EPC meta model and can be represented by a Function, an Event, an Operator, a Process Interface.

subclasses.name: Connector
subclasses.description: A connector determines the behavior of the process in case its control ?ow is split up into or joined from several execution branches.

subclasses.name: AND
subclasses.description:
All incoming pathways required to proceed along the flow
All outgoing pathways must be followed
Used to divide/rejoin tasks/flows which happen in parallel with another, rather than in a strict sequence

subclasses.name: OR
subclasses.description: At least one of the possible process paths must be followed.

subclasses.name: XOR
subclasses.description: Exactly one of the possible process paths must be followed.

subclasses.name: Event
subclasses.description: An event illustrates the fact that a process object has taken on a business relevant state influencing the further procedure of a process. Unlike a function, which is a time consuming occurrence, an event is related to one point in time. Therefore, it is used to describe an event or status in the process flow. The object is mandatory for: EPC start and EPC end or after x (xor), v (or).

subclasses.name: End Event
subclasses.description: Denotes the event element that stands at the end of a branch in the process flow and thus, ends the process flow branch or the total process.

subclasses.name: Start Event
subclasses.description: Denotes the event that stands at the beginning of a branch in the process flow and thus, triggers the execution of this branch or the total process.

subclasses.name: Function
subclasses.description: The function type represents several action elements as task, process interfaces or business process activities.

subclasses.name: Business Process Activity
subclasses.description: A Business Process (BP) Activity is a part of a Business Process containing one or more sub Business Processes or a Process Flow.

subclasses.name: Rule
subclasses.description: Rules allow to model alternative, exclusive alternative and parallel process flows.

subclasses.name: Output
subclasses.description: The amount of energy, work, goods, or services produced by a machine, factory, company, or an individual in a period.

subclasses.name: Process
subclasses.description: A collection of subprocesses that meet a specific business objective. E.g. Perform Sourcing or Purchase Materials and Services

subclasses.name: Screen
subclasses.description: A transaction in SAP is described as a screen. Here, they represent the actions undertaken in the application SAP to perform a function in a process flow.

subclasses.name: Value Added Chain Diagram
subclasses.description:
A Value-Added Chain is a process that represents an element of the process chain. A process hierarchy can be realized by hierarchically structuring value chains, thus modeling business areas, process groups, business processes and business process variants using the sam notation.
House: represents enabler processes.

name: Product Lobe
description:
A product is a tangible or intangible item or service that is created, manufactured, or offered to fulfill a need or desire of customers.

The Product Lobe maps the notions of Customer Part Number Specification, Design Target, Integration Level, Main Power Device Type, Motor Type and Organization.

subclasses.name: Product
subclasses.description:
A product is any tangible output or service that is a result of a process and that is intended for delivery to a customer or end user. A product is something that is produced with effort (e.g. by mechanical or industrial processes) and sold to a customer. A product is either tangible (physical product) or intangible (service). A solution is a combination of products which is sold to a customer. Thereby, a solution solves a problem or fulfills a customer need.

The superclass of all classes describing products or services types, either by nature or purpose. Examples for such subclasses are "TV set", "vacuum cleaner", etc. An instance of this class can be either an actual product or service (gr:Individual), a placeholder instance for unknown instances of a mass-produced commodity (gr:SomeItems), or a model / prototype specification (gr:ProductOrServiceModel). When in doubt, use gr:SomeItems. Examples:
a) MyCellphone123, i.e. my personal, tangible cell phone (gr:Individual)
b) Siemens1234, i.e. the Siemens cell phone make and model 1234 (gr:ProductOrServiceModel)
c) dummyCellPhone123 as a placeholder for actual instances of a certain kind of cell phones (gr:SomeItems)

subclasses.name: Angle Sensor
subclasses.description: Infineon offers a family of angle sensors based on integrated Magneto Resistive (ixMR) technologies. Technologies include today iGMR and AMR. The sensors detect the orientation of an applied magnetic field by measuring sine and cosine angle components with monolithically integrated magneto resistive elements. ixMR technology is now widely used in automotive and industrial applications and provides a wide range of benefits. Our iAMR sensors are ideal for applications with the highest accuracy requirements. Our iAMR technology offers best performance over temperature, lifetime and magnetic field range. They are pre-calibrated and ready to use.

subclasses.name: Hall Switch
subclasses.description: The sensor provides an easy-to-use and cost effective solution for position sensing applications, requiring high temperature stability of the magnetic threshold. Today the market demands smaller and more energy efficient Hall switches. To satisfy the needs of more compact designs and environmental legislation  with a high quality product is very difficult. Infineon offers attractive pricing, reliable supply, benchmark quality and excellent design-in support to contribute to the customers success.

subclasses.name: Linear Hall Sensor
subclasses.description:
Measure the vertical component of a magnetic field and outputs a signal that is directly proportional to the magnetic field. These programmable linear Hall sensors come with different interface options. Our family of TLE499x linear Hall ICs is tailored to the needs of highly accurate angular and linear position detection and current measurement applications.
Each product measures the vertical component of a magnetic field and outputs a signal that is directly proportional to the magnetic field. These programmable linear Hall sensors come with different interface options.

of linear, rotation or 3 dimensional movements.

subclasses.name: Magnetic Speed Sensor
subclasses.description: The  magnetic speed sensors are designed to measure speed in safety and powertrain applications such as speedometers, ABS, camshafts/crankshafts and automatic transmissions. They are also used in similar applications in the industrial sector. The sensors use a ferromagnetic gear tooth or encoder structure to measure linear or rotational speed and position.

A sealed capacitive sensing element is used for pressure measurement, guaranteeing high precision and accuracy across temperature changes. The small package and low energy consumption make  DPS310 ideal for mobile applications and wearable devices.

subclasses.name: Integrated Pressure Sensor

The barometric air pressure (BAP) is an important parameter to compute the air-fuel ratio provided to the engine and for controlling spark advance to optimize engine efficiency. In automotive applications where high production volumes are common there is substantial interest in precision, low-cost and fully integrated sensors.

Whether you require increased range coverage for outdoor lighting or a small form factor solution to enable soft landing in your multicopter our radar provides you with the ability to make your motion sensing applications perform in a way previously not possible. The BGT24M/L family is the largest and highest integrated 24GHz ISM band radar transceiver family currently in the market, providing a range of different transmitter and receiver channel configurations, supporting different application requirements. the sensor allows a Long range distance detection of moving objects up to 30 m and a wide range speed detection up to more than ±100 km/h.

subclasses.name: Quality Complaint 8D
subclasses.description: Report out to the Customer on the technical complaint or Issue as reported by a customer.

subclasses.name: Step D1
subclasses.description: The objective of process step D1 is to determine a sponsor, a team leader and the best possible team to solve the problem in a specific case

subclasses.name: Step D2
subclasses.description: The objective of the process step D2 is to understand the problem with regard to its interconnections and transfer the identified non-conformity into a specific, fact-based problem description. A problem description is a simple, precise statement about the item and the non-conformity, whose cause is not known. It should be as accurate as possible, and the problem environment should also be described if applicable (e.g. the processes/components involved within a complex system). The core of the problem is to be identified and quantified. All necessary data are available and analyzed sufficiently so that the extent of the problem (number of parts concerned, versions, vehicles, etc.) can be described in a manner that is understandable.

subclasses.name: Step D3
subclasses.description: The objective of D3 is to define the containment actions in order to fully eliminate the impact of the problem on external and internal customers. The containment actions have to be implemented and their effectiveness ensured until the implemented corrective actions (D6) have been validated. All containment actions serve to limit immediate losses, and are based on specific requirements (software, services, hardware, etc.)

subclasses.name: Step D4
subclasses.description: In process step D4, the actual causes of the underlying problem - the root causes - are determined and verified based on the problem description (D2), the Is/Is-Not analysis and taking into consideration the findings from the containment actions (D3). The objective is to identify both the technical root causes and the systemic root causes (see glossary) for the occurrence of the failure and the non-detection of the failure.

subclasses.name: Step D5
subclasses.description: The objective of process step D5 is the development, selection and verification of corrective actions to eliminate the technical and systemic root causes for the occurrence and nondetection identified in D4 (root cause analysis). Corrective actions are selected on the basis of proven effectiveness while taking their efficiency into account. Evidence of effectiveness must be documented. The optimum corrective actions with long-term effect are to be selected. Suitable tests, for example, are to be used to demonstrate that the selected corrective actions solve the problem permanently and do not have any undesirable effects. The outcome is an approved action plan with established deadlines, resource plan and responsibilities for the selected corrective actions

subclasses.name: Step D6
subclasses.description: The objective of D6 is the implementation of the selected permanent corrective actions. The permanent corrective actions are validated and long-term results are observed. The containment actions will be removed/lifted after the implementation and validation of the permanent corrective actions.

subclasses.name: Step D7
subclasses.description: The objective of the D7 is to identify and document actions that ensure the permanent prevention of the identified root causes for similar products or processes by adapting the management system in the sense of standardization. The result is the preparation and transfer of acquired information to other processes, such as the lessons learned process.

subclasses.name: Step D8
subclasses.description: The purpose of process step D8 is to conclude the team's work, to acknowledge the performance of individuals and the team, and to release the team from the task. The result is the completed 8D report.

The Semiconductor Development lobe of the Digital Reference models the Current Work In Progress, Cycle Time and Delivery Commitment, EPA, Equipment and Equipent Group, and Event Calendar.

subclasses.name: Location
subclasses.description:
LOCATION refers to a physical or virtual place where an action, process, or activity occurs, playing a critical role in the execution of tasks within the supply chain, production, and planning systems.

•	Logistics perspective: A location signifies the point where responsibility, ownership, or risk transitions between parties during the transfer of goods or services.
•	Demand Fulfillment Perspective: A location represents the origin or destination of demand-related processes, such as the point of product dispatch, delivery to customers, or storage of inventory to meet customer needs.
•	Planning Perspective: Locations are key inputs for planning activities, representing the physical sites or nodes in the supply chain (e.g., factories, warehouses, or distribution centers) where resources, capacity, or inventory must be allocated.
•	Semiconductor Production Perspective: In manufacturing, a location indicates a specific site where production steps take place, such as fabrication, assembly, or testing.

LOCATIONS are fundamental to managing supply chain efficiency, tracking material flow, coordinating production processes, and ensuring timely fulfillment of customer orders.
