The “Cycle Time Commitment” entity helps controlling the WIP
via the release plan. (strategy entity)

subclasses.name: Delivery Commitment
subclasses.description: The "Delivery Commitment" directly corresponds to the release plans and cycle time commitments introduced in the corresponding entities.

subclasses.name: Demand Snapshot
subclasses.description: The “Demand” entity stores redundant demand at every product level. (snapshot entity)

subclasses.name: EPA
subclasses.description: The EPA is a product identifier referring to the associated process.

subclasses.name: Event Calendar
subclasses.description: In the “Event Calendar” tracing entity, certain events like planned facility shutdowns, etc. can be scheduled

subclasses.name: Public Holiday
subclasses.description: Special period of time when some processes may not take place or some constrains may occure

subclasses.name: Fab
subclasses.description: The “Fab” entity depicts the fab as a technological and physical production unit. (master entity)

subclasses.name: Furnace Process
subclasses.description: Sequence of interdependent and linked procedures which, at every stage, consume one or more resources (employee time, energy, machines, money) to convert inputs (data, material, parts, etc.) into outputs. These outputs then serve as inputs for the next stage until a known goal or end result is reached.

subclasses.name: Tempering
subclasses.description: The tempering process is a type of heat treatment applied by the furnace. The process has the effect of toughening by lessing brittleness and reducing internal stresses.

subclasses.name: Lot
subclasses.description: The Lot represents manufacturing unit (e.g. in the semicondutor industry in Frontend this often consists of 25 or 50 wafers).

subclasses.name: Lot Event
subclasses.description: The Lot Event  tracing entity gives the history of lot events. e.g. Hold events, Split events, Merge events, etc. (tracing entities).

subclasses.name: Lot Size
subclasses.description: A measure or quantity increment acceptable to or specified by the party offering to buy or sell. Used also as an alternative term for lot quantity.

subclasses.name: Mask
subclasses.description: A transparent (glass or quartz) plate covered with an array of patterns used in making an IC. Each pattern consists of opaque and transparent areas that define the size and shape of all circuit and device elements. The mask is used to expose selected areas, and defines the areas to be processed. Masks may use emulsion, chrome, iron oxide, silicon or other material to produce the opaque areas.

subclasses.name: Material Transfer Matrix
subclasses.description: A material transfer matrix estimates the duration of material from on to another equipment.

subclasses.name: Operation
subclasses.description: The master entity “Operation” depicts the generic behavior of a single process step. Each operation has a foreign key relation to equipment and to route which means that the operation is required by the specific routes and requires a specific equipment. (workflow descriptive master entity)

subclasses.name: Operator
subclasses.description: A user that interacts with the equipment only to the degree necessary for the equipment to perform its intended function.

object_properties.name: is responsible for planning work center

subclasses.name: Owner
subclasses.description: An owner is the entity that has the highest level of access authority or legal right to a system or equipment.

subclasses.name: Planning Work Center
subclasses.description: Semiconductor wafers arrive at the planning work center according to a Poisson process in lots with a certain unit size. The planning work center X48- can process three different products which arrive in four different classes.

subclasses.name: Priority Class
subclasses.description: Each lot is characterized by a product type and a priority class. The priority classes are listed as follows: development, hot, productive, rocket and timecoupling.

subclasses.name: Development
subclasses.description: These lots have the same maxium waiting time as standard lots, however they are put before the standard lots.

subclasses.name: Hot
subclasses.description: These lots are processed after a certain maximum waiting time which is shorter than the maximum waiting time of standard lots. In general, for all classes, if there is more than one product type waiting.

subclasses.name: Productive
subclasses.description: The standard lots, also referred to as Productive (Prod) lots, are the most common lot type and have no priority.

subclasses.name: Rocket
subclasses.description: Rocket lots are processed immediately if a machine has free capacity. The remaining furnace space is then filled up with lots of the same product.

subclasses.name: Time Coupling
subclasses.description: Lots of this type are requested by the next machine in the production line in irregular intervals. Special chemical characteristics require the lot being further processed immediately after the furnace operation. Thus, the downstram machines keep capacity free for the resulting time slot. timecoupling can be turned on or off. if it is on all lots are processed no matter how many are waiting and if not they wait.

subclasses.name: Process
subclasses.description: Sequence of interdependent and linked procedures which, at every stage, consume one or more resources (employee time, energy, machines, money) to convert inputs (data, material, parts, etc.) into outputs. These outputs then serve as inputs for the next stage until a known goal or end result is reached.

subclasses.name: Process Class
subclasses.description: A Process Class is the second hierarchy level in the Technology Catalogue and is a subset of top hierarchy level "Technology Class". A Process Class is defined by the device category and its generation or wafer diameter.

subclasses.name: Process Flow
subclasses.description: A wafer technology is defined as a manufacturing process flow on wafer level including wafer test and pre-assembly which creates one device (discrete technology) or a set of different devices (IC technology) to be used in a product.

subclasses.name: Process Group
subclasses.description: A Process Group is the third hierarchy level in the Technology Catalogue and a subset of the Process Class. A Process Group is defined by the device type and its generation (eventually voltage class) or wafer diameter

subclasses.name: Process Line
subclasses.description: A Process Line is the forth hierarchy level in the Technology Catalogue and is a subset of Process Group. A Process Line is defined by WHAT is produced in detail

subclasses.name: Product Level
subclasses.description: In the "product level" entity, the aggregation of elements enables the grouping of products and defines the relationship between products and groups at different hierarchy levels. This supports planning, logistics, modeling, forecasting and reporting.

subclasses.name: Product Level 2
subclasses.description: The product levels 3 to 1 are aggregated levels that are based on information from product level 4. (hierarchal aggregation level)

subclasses.name: Product Level 3
subclasses.description:
The static bottlenecks are determined in the “Product Level 3” master entity
because the mid capacity planning is done on this first aggregated product level. There is no big difference in capacity from the aggregated level 3 product to its child level 4 products. (hierarchal aggregation level)

subclasses.name: Production Request
subclasses.description: Production requests definte what the facilities need to produce when and in what quantity.

subclasses.name: Purge
subclasses.description: purge' is the application of an intert gas, or gas mixture, to the OD or ID surface of the weld joint to displace non-inert atmospheric gases. A block purge is a non-flowing purge with positive pressure.

subclasses.name: Release Plan
subclasses.description: The “Release Plan” entity shows the quantity planned to be released to a fab or facility. (strategy entity)

subclasses.name: Robot
subclasses.description: The robot loads and unloads the lots from the WIP station into the furnace. Robot can load the furnace while another boat is processd by the tool.

subclasses.name: Route
subclasses.description: The master entity “Route” describes the structure of a workflow out of operations. Every product uses a specific route in its value stream, i.e. the complete sequence of operations with all mandatory and optional operations necessary to complete the product. A route makes use of the single operations. (workflow descriptive master entity)

subclasses.name: Shift
subclasses.description: Each workshop has a certain technical and operational workforce organized in shifts described in the “Shift” entity.

subclasses.name: Simulation Part
subclasses.description: A simulation part helps to identify the same product in different locations. They are visible in Product Structures. This is a simulation entity and not a form of production/planning.

subclasses.name: Simulation Route
subclasses.description: A simulation route (AKA workroute) represents a sequence of process steps in manufacutring (mainly at wafer fab). This is a simulation entity and not a form of production/planning.

subclasses.name: Supply Chain
subclasses.description: The entity “Supply Chain” describes the supply chain from the topmost level with all possible material flow edges, referring on the FabIDs (master entity)

subclasses.name: Target Costs
subclasses.description: The target costs entity is the final cost of a product or service that must be achieved in order to generate the desired level of sales revenue and income or due to contractual agreements.

datatype_properties.name: WIP costs per unit and time unit

subclasses.name: Target Revenue
subclasses.description: The target revenue is the amount of income a company wants to generate for the current accounting period.

subclasses.name: Target Service Level
subclasses.description: The target service level is a performance indicator expressing the percentage of orders satisfied.

subclasses.name: Time Constraints
subclasses.description: As single operations can set the lot to a time-critical state, time constraints can ensure that the operation setting it to an uncritical state is not delayed. Also the other case where certain time has to be spent between two operations can be covered with this master entity. (workflow deswcriptive master entities)

subclasses.name: Tool
subclasses.description: A tool is any pieve of semiconductor fabrication or inspection equipment designed to process wafers. Often used synonymously with equipment in the silicon wafer processing industry.

subclasses.name: Furnace
subclasses.description: Each furnace consists of two chambers with one tool in each chamber.

subclasses.name: Work In Progress Station
subclasses.description: Work in Progress (WIP) processing occurs here. WIP refers to the units of production that have been released into the factory, but have not yet been scrapped, have not been sent our for external rework, and have not finished processing through all of the production steps.

subclasses.name: Workshop
subclasses.description: The overall organizational working structures within the fabs is described in the entity “Workshop” (master entity)

subclasses.name: Chemical Polishing
subclasses.description: The chemical polishing process or chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) is a process whereby a chemical reaction increases the mechanical removal rate of a material. CMP is commonly used to polish off high spots on wafers or films deposited on wafers, flattening the film or wafer, referred to as planarization. The chemical reaction that increases the mechanical removal rate is commonly tailored to provide a higher removal rate of one material versus another material. The chemical action in CMP helps to achieve higher selectivity's of one material to another than a strictly mechanical process would provide.

subclasses.name: Deposition
subclasses.description: The deposition process, or chemical vapor deposition (CVD) is a process whereby a fiolm is deposited by reacting chemicals together in the gaseous or vapor phase to form a film. The gases or vapors utilized for CVD are compounds that contain the element to be deposited and that may be inducted to react with a substrate or other gas(es) to deposit a film. The CVD reactoin may be thermally activated, plasma induced, plasma enhanced CVD or activated by light in photon induced CVD.

subclasses.name: Diffusion
subclasses.description: Diffusion is a process whereby a substance redistributes from an area of relatively high concentration to an area of relatively low concentration due to random thermal motion. The larger the concentration gradient the faster diffusion occurs for a given temperature, conversely, the higher the temperature the faster diffusion occurs for a given concentration gradient.

subclasses.name: Dry Etching
subclasses.description: Dry etching is a process whereby etching is accomplished by a reactive gas as opposed to a liquid. Dry etching techniques include plasma etch, reactive ion etch, magnetically enhanced reactive ion etch, inductively coupled plasma, electron spin resonance, etc.

subclasses.name: Implantation
subclasses.description: Implantation or Ion Implantation is a technique where ions are accelerated to a higher energy and speed an injected into a semiconductor. The dominant techniques for introducing dopants into a semiconductor.

subclasses.name: Lithography
subclasses.description: The lithography process is the key process in frontend. This consists of the following steps: a photo resisting layer is spun on a wafer, then exposed through the mask, then developed, then showing the effect on the open places, and then final deletion of the photo resisting material leaves only the remaining structure on the water. after some time for deposition, these steps are repeated up to 35 times.

subclasses.name: Sputtering
subclasses.description: The sputtering process, or physical vapor deposition (PVD) is the most used layering process today. Here gas atoms, mostly argon, strike out atoms from the cathode I an electric field which then form a thin film on the wafer surface.

subclasses.name: Wet Etching
subclasses.description: Wet Etching is the process of removing material-etching, through the use of chemical activity.

name: Sensor Lobe
description:
A sensor is a device or component that detects and measures physical, chemical or environmental parameters and converts them into electrical signals for futher analysis or use.

The Sensor lobes models the notion of a System and its Deployment.
It maps the topics of Actuation, Feature of Interest, Input, Mounting Style, Observation and Observation Collection, and  Output.
It also represents Platform, Procedure, Property, Relationship Nature, Result, Sample Relationship, Sampling, Sensing Type, and Stimulus.

subclasses.name: Observation Collection
subclasses.description: An Observation Collection has at least one member, and may have one of any of the other seven properties mentioned in restrictions.

subclasses.name: Actuation
subclasses.description: An Actuation carries out an (Actuation) Procedure to change the state of the world using an Actuator.

subclasses.name: Feature Of Interest
subclasses.description: The thing whose property is being estimated or calculated in the course of an Observation to arrive at a Result or whose property is being manipulated by an Actuator, or which is being sampled or transformed in an act of Sampling.

subclasses.name: Sample
subclasses.description: A Sample is the result from an act of Sampling.

subclasses.name: Observation
subclasses.description: Act of carrying out an (Observation) Procedure to estimate or calculate a value of a property of a FeatureOfInterest. Links to a Sensor to describe what made the Observation and how; links to an ObservableProperty to describe what the result is an estimate of, and to a FeatureOfInterest to detail what that property was associated with.

subclasses.name: Platform
subclasses.description: A Platform is an entity that hosts other entities, particularly Sensors, Actuators, Samplers, and other Platforms.

subclasses.name: Procedure
subclasses.description: A workflow, protocol, plan, algorithm, or computational method specifying how to make an Observation, create a Sample, or make a change to the state of the world (via an Actuator). A Procedure is re-usable, and might be involved in many Observations, Samplings, or Actuations. It explains the steps to be carried out to arrive at reproducible results.

subclasses.name: Result
subclasses.description: The Result of an Observation, Actuation, or act of Sampling. To store an observation's simple result value one can use the hasSimpleResult property.

subclasses.name: Sampling
subclasses.description: An act of Sampling carries out a sampling Procedure to create or transform one or more samples.

subclasses.name: Relationship Nature
subclasses.description: Nature of a relationship (between samples) - Members of this class indicate the nature of a relationship between two samples.

subclasses.name: Sample Relationship
subclasses.description: Members of this class represent a relationship between a sample and another.

subclasses.name: Deployment
subclasses.description: Describes the Deployment of one or more Systems for a particular purpose. Deployment may be done on a Platform.

subclasses.name: Input
subclasses.description: Any information that is provided to a Procedure for its use.

subclasses.name: Output
subclasses.description: Any information that is reported from a Procedure.

subclasses.name: Property
subclasses.description: A quality of an entity. An aspect of an entity that is intrinsic to and cannot exist without the entity.

subclasses.name: Actuatable Property
subclasses.description: An actuatable quality (property, characteristic) of a FeatureOfInterest.

subclasses.name: Observable Property
subclasses.description: An observable quality (property, characteristic) of a FeatureOfInterest.

subclasses.name: Condition
subclasses.description: Used to specify ranges for qualities that act as Condition on a Systems' operation.

subclasses.name: Operating Property
subclasses.description: An identifiable characteristic that represents how the System operates under the specified Conditions. May describe power ranges, power sources, standard configurations, attachments and the like.

subclasses.name: Maintenance Schedule
subclasses.description: Schedule of maintenance for a System in the specified Conditions.

subclasses.name: Operating Power Range
subclasses.description: Power range in which System is expected to operate in the specified.

subclasses.name: Operating Range
subclasses.description:
"Describes normal OperatingProperties of a System under some specified Conditions. For example, to the power requirement or maintenance schedule of a System under a specified temperature range.
In the absence of OperatingProperties, it simply describes the Conditions in which a System is expected to operate."

subclasses.name: Survival Property
subclasses.description: An identifiable characteristic that represents the extent of the System's useful life under the specified Conditions. May describe for example total battery life or number of recharges, or, for Sensors that are used only a fixed number of times, the number of Observations that can be made before the sensing capability is depleted.

subclasses.name: Battery Lifetime
subclasses.description: Total useful life of a System's battery in the specified Conditions.

subclasses.name: System Lifetime
subclasses.description: The System continues to operate as defined using SystemCapability. If, however, the SurvivalRange is violated, the System is 'damaged' and SystemCapability specifications may no longer hold.

subclasses.name: Survival Range
subclasses.description:
"Describes SurvivalProperties of a System under some specified Conditions. For example, the lifetime of a System under a specified temperature range.
In the absence of SurvivalProperties, simply describes the Conditions a System can be exposed to without damage. For example, the temperature range a System can withstand before being considered damaged."

subclasses.name: System Capability
subclasses.description: Describes normal measurement, actuation, sampling properties such as accuracy, range, precision, etc. Of a System under some specified Conditions such as temperature range. The capabilities specified here are those that affect the primary purpose of the System, while those in OperatingRange represent the system's normal operating environment, including Conditions that don't affect the Observations or the Actuations.

subclasses.name: System Property
subclasses.description: An identifiable and observable characteristic that represents the system's ability to operate its primary purpose: a sensor to make Observations, an Actuator to make Actuations, or a Sampler to make Sampling.

subclasses.name: Oversampling Rate
subclasses.description: Specifies the number of sensor measurements used internally to generate one sensor output result. (Oversampling rate = OSR)

subclasses.name: Accuracy
subclasses.description: The closeness of agreement between the Result of an Observation (resp. The command of an Actuation) and the true value of the observed ObservableProperty (resp. Of the acted on ActuableProperty) under the defined Conditions.

subclasses.name: Actuation Range
subclasses.description: The range of property values that can be the Result of an Actuation under the defined Conditions.

subclasses.name: Detection Limit
subclasses.description: An observed value for which the probability of falsely claiming the absence of a component in a material is beta, given a probability alpha of falsely claiming its presence.

subclasses.name: Drift
subclasses.description: As a Sensor Property: a continuous or incremental change in the reported values of Observations over time for an unchanging Property under the defined Conditions. As an Actuator Property: a continuous or incremental change in the true value of the acted on ActuableProperty over time for an unchanging command under the defined Conditions.

subclasses.name: Frequency
subclasses.description: The smallest possible time between one Observation, Actuation, or Sampling and the next, under the defined Conditions.

subclasses.name: Latency
subclasses.description: The time between a command for an Observation and the Sensor providing a Result, under the defined Conditions.

subclasses.name: Measurement Range
subclasses.description: The set of values that the Sensor can return as the Result of an Observation under the defined Conditions with the defined system properties.

subclasses.name: Precision
subclasses.description: As a sensor capability: The closeness of agreement between replicate Observations on an unchanged or similar quality value: i.e., a measure of a Sensor's ability to consistently reproduce an Observation, under the defined Conditions.

subclasses.name: Resolution
subclasses.description: As an actuator capability: The closeness of agreement between replicate Actuations for an unchanged or similar command: i.e., a measure of an Actuator's ability to consistently reproduce an Actuations, under the defined Conditions.

subclasses.name: Response Time
subclasses.description: As a Sensor Property: the time between a (step) change in the value of an observed ObservableProperty and a Sensor (possibly with specified error) 'settling' on an observed value, under the defined Conditions.

subclasses.name: Selectivity
subclasses.description: As an Actuator Property: the time between a (step) change in the command of an Actuator and the 'settling' of the value of the acted on ActuatableProperty, under the defined Conditions.

subclasses.name: Sensitivity
subclasses.description: As a Sensor Property: Sensitivity is the quotient of the change in a Result of Observations and the corresponding change in a value of an ObservableProperty being observed, under the defined Conditions.

subclasses.name: Stimulus
subclasses.description: An event in the real world that 'triggers' the Sensor. The properties associated to the Stimulus may be different to the eventual observed ObservableProperty. It is the event, not the object, that triggers the Sensor.

subclasses.name: Stocks
subclasses.description: A supply of something for use or sale

subclasses.name: DC
subclasses.description: A DC Facility represents a finished goods store.

subclasses.name: Die Bank
subclasses.description: A die bank is an area in production where (usually) tested wafers are stored waiting for disposition and further production.

subclasses.name: WIP
subclasses.description:
Work In Progress (WIP) includes the unfinished items for products in a production process.
These items are not yet completed but either just being fabricated or waiting in a queue for further processing.

subclasses.name: Submodel
subclasses.description: Describe the different types of data related to the I4.0 asset

subclasses.name: Energy Efficiency
subclasses.description: Specifies some details regarding energy efficiency. These can also be supplied by sensors.

subclasses.name: MES Connection
subclasses.description: Connects the station to a higher-level MES system via a small number of properties. Specifies whether the station is producing, ready for production, has a fault or is undergoing maintenance, for example.

subclasses.name: Sensor Measurement
subclasses.description: Measurement performed by a sensor

subclasses.name: Structure
subclasses.description: The way in which the parts of a system or object are arranged or organized, or a system arranged in this way

subclasses.name: Transport Interface
subclasses.description: Transport_Interface - represents the data models and interfaces associated with the transportation and movement of goods within the supply chain. This includes data related to logistics, shipping, and distribution, as well as the various modes of transport such as trucks, trains, ships, and aircraft. By providing a standardized framework for capturing and exchanging information about transportation processes and assets, the Transport_Interface subclass enables more efficient and reliable supply chain operations.

subclasses.name: System
subclasses.description: System is a unit of abstraction for pieces of infrastructure that implement Procedures. A System may have components, its subsystems, which are other systems.

subclasses.name: Actuator
subclasses.description: A device that is used by, or implements, an (Actuation) Procedure that changes the state of the world.

subclasses.name: Sampler
subclasses.description: A device that is used by, or implements, a Sampling Procedure to create or transform one or more samples.

subclasses.name: Sensor
subclasses.description: Device, agent (including humans), or software (simulation) involved in, or implementing, a Procedure. Sensors respond to a stimulus, e.g., a change in the environment, or input data composed from the results of prior Observations, and generate a Result. Sensors can be hosted by Platforms.

subclasses.name: Mounting Style
subclasses.description: Each sensor has a specific mounting style. A mounting style can either be a "SMDSMT" or "Through Hole".

subclasses.name: Sensing Type
subclasses.description: The sensing type of a semiconductor solution determines whether a semiconductor solution contains a sensor ("WithSensor") or not ("WithoutSensor).

name: Supply Chain Lobe
description:
Supply chain refers to a network of interconnected organizations, activities, resources, and technologies involved in the production, distribution, and delivery of goods or services from the source to end consumer.

The Supply Chain lobe models the Aggregated Capacity Group.

 It represents the notions of Action, Allocated Available To Promise, Allocation, Available To Promise, Confirmation, Capacity Bottleneck, Contact Person Data, Location, Marketing Demand, nEWs, Offer, Open Oder and Open Order Book.

It depicts the Order and its Change Request, Confirmation, Line Item, Reschedule, Schedule Line.

It represents the General Customers, the notion of Customer and its Data, Logistics Management Representative, Plant, Plant Data.
It also maps the topics of Prioritized Demand and Orders, Products, Promise, Sales Supplier, Seller, Supplier and its Data, Supply, Supply Demand Match and Picture, Target Allocation, Transfer Action, and User Action.

subclasses.name: Customer
subclasses.description:
CUSTOMER is a person, organization, or business entity that generates demand by placing an order or making a request for a specific product or service. A customer may also fulfill their obligations by facilitating payment for the goods or services received.

Customers can be categorized into two main types: 
•	External Customers: Entities outside the organization that purchase goods or services, often governed by agreements like Incoterms.
•	Internal Customers: Stakeholders or departments within the organization that raise internal demand for products or services to support internal processes.

A customer interacts with the organization through actions such as order placement, demand generation, and the completion of financial transactions. Customers are central to both demand creation in the supply chain and the fulfillment processes that ensure the delivery of goods or services.

subclasses.name: End Customer
subclasses.description: The final person, organization, or business entity that ultimately receives or uses a product or service at the end of the supply chain.

subclasses.name: Private Customer
subclasses.description: Private Customer is an entity, such as a business, organisation, or individual, that engages in a direct and often exclusive transactional relationship with a semiconductor manufacturer, supplier, or service provider. This customer typically operates outside of the public marketplace or general distribution channels, relying on custom solutions, specialised services, or dedicated resources tailored to meet specific requirements.

subclasses.name: Order
subclasses.description: DF and Planning definition: An ORDER contains at least one order position. An ORDER has an order type and is associated to DEMAND.

subclasses.name: Customer Order
subclasses.description: This is an order that is initiated by a customer.

subclasses.name: Replenishment Order
subclasses.description: This is an order that is initiated by an internal request of the semiconductor manufacturer to produce the order according to a MTS strategy. The replenishment order can be divided into different sub order types, depending on the purpose of order creation.

subclasses.name: Split Order
subclasses.description: This is an order that results from a split delivery. When an order position of an order is delivered in several portions, each portion starting from the second one is considered as a separate suborder which is called scheduled order position. The original order also exists after the split.

subclasses.name: Buffer Stock Order
subclasses.description: Buffer Stock Order reserves stock for fluctuating customer demands.

subclasses.name: Consignment Order
subclasses.description:
Consignment Stock is a logistics concept where the supplier (Vendor) owned goods are stored at a customer location.

The supplier (Vendor) is responsible to maintain his stock within a defined min/max level.

subclasses.name: EDI Forecast
subclasses.description: The EDI Forecast Universe is a Data Mart that was started in 2010 (?) to support Forecast Accuracy  analysis

subclasses.name: Standard Order
subclasses.description: EDI or manually entered, can be shipped, can contain several products.

subclasses.name: Sales Channel
subclasses.description: a route or intermediary through which products or services are sold

subclasses.name: Supplier
subclasses.description: A SUPPLIER is an entity fulfilling a demand for a specific product or service.

subclasses.name: Supplier Data
subclasses.description: Information about a supplier.

subclasses.name: Allocated Available To Promise
subclasses.description: ALLOCATED AVAILABLE TO PROMISE is when scarce ATP quantities are allocated to different customer classes or customers. The resulting supply reservations are called allocated ATP (AATP) quantities.

subclasses.name: Available To Promise
subclasses.description: AVAILABLE TO PROMISE is the part of the inventory and projected supply that can be used to fulfill customer orders is called ATP.

subclasses.name: Customer Class
subclasses.description: CUSTOMER CLASS is the set of all customers is divided into different priority classes or segments based on certain criteria like profitability or importance of customer.

subclasses.name: External Customer
subclasses.description: A customer classification for persons, organizations, or business entities outside Infineon that purchase or request its products or services through demand fulfillment.

subclasses.name: Internal Customer
subclasses.description: A customer classification for stakeholders, departments, or organizational units within the supplying organization that generate demand for products or services supporting internal processes.

subclasses.name: Delivery Concept
subclasses.description: The DELIVERY CONCEPT defines the terms and conditions for delivering an order to the customer. Partial and split delivery has to be taken into account.

subclasses.name: Complete Delivery
subclasses.description: The normal case is that an order is completely delivered.

subclasses.name: Partial Delivery
subclasses.description: It can be allowed that only parts of an order position of an order are delivered. Therefore, the customer is willing to waive parts of quantity belonging to an order position.

subclasses.name: Split Delivery
subclasses.description: It can be allowed that order positions of an order are delivered in several portions.

subclasses.name: Demand
subclasses.description: DEMAND is a supply chain or production request for a specific product, product group or service. Either demand exists explicitly in form of customer need (e.g. orders or EDI forecast) or implicitly as expected customer need.

subclasses.name: Demand Class
subclasses.description: The DEMAND CLASS is dividing the demand into priority classes.

subclasses.name: Firm Order Demand
subclasses.description: This is a special demand class that is used for demand that is required to fulfill already committed/accepted orders.

subclasses.name: Forecasted Demand
subclasses.description: This is a special demand class that is used for the projection of future demand.

subclasses.name: Inventory Replenishment Demand
subclasses.description: This is a special demand class that is used for replenishment of safety stock.

subclasses.name: Demand Priority
subclasses.description: DEMAND PRIORITY is the concept that is used to describe the different importance level of a demand. The demand priority can be assigned independently from the demand class.

subclasses.name: Location
subclasses.description:
LOCATION refers to a physical or virtual place where an action, process, or activity occurs, playing a critical role in the execution of tasks within the supply chain, production, and planning systems.

•	Logistics perspective: A location signifies the point where responsibility, ownership, or risk transitions between parties during the transfer of goods or services.
•	Demand Fulfillment Perspective: A location represents the origin or destination of demand-related processes, such as the point of product dispatch, delivery to customers, or storage of inventory to meet customer needs.
•	Planning Perspective: Locations are key inputs for planning activities, representing the physical sites or nodes in the supply chain (e.g., factories, warehouses, or distribution centers) where resources, capacity, or inventory must be allocated.
•	Semiconductor Production Perspective: In manufacturing, a location indicates a specific site where production steps take place, such as fabrication, assembly, or testing.

LOCATIONS are fundamental to managing supply chain efficiency, tracking material flow, coordinating production processes, and ensuring timely fulfillment of customer orders.

subclasses.name: Order Position
subclasses.description: An ORDER POSITION refers to a product specification, a product quantity, and a desired delivery date. Each order position has a status and belongs to an order.

subclasses.name: Production Strategy
subclasses.description: The PRODUCTION STRATEGY determining which portions of a supply chain should operate in make to stock (MTS) mode, where production is driven by the replenishment of inventories at specific locations, and which in make to order (MTO) mode, where production is initiated to fulfill specific customer orders. The production strategy is related to the question where the customer order decoupling point (CODP), also referred to as the push-pull interface (or boundary) has to be placed. The CODP denotes the point in the supply chain where material is dedicated to a specific customer order to the degree that it cannot be used for another.

subclasses.name: Assemble To Order (ATO)
subclasses.description: In the case of ATO, products are produced forecast-driven until the point right before it comes to the assembly. Starting from there, the production continues based on a customer order.

subclasses.name: Make To Order (MTO)
subclasses.description: This is a strategy where production is initiated to fulfill specific customer orders. This strategy is characterized by an order-driven production.

subclasses.name: Make To Stock (MTS)
subclasses.description: This is a strategy where production is driven by the replenishment of inventories at specific locations. Products are produced forecast-driven until they are completely finished in the case of MTS.

subclasses.name: Supply
subclasses.description: SUPPLY is the total amount of specific products or services that is available to customers. Supply has the dimensions quantity, time, location, product, including aggregation of all dimensions. Supply is defined as inventory or plan replenishment.

subclasses.name: Supply Chain
subclasses.description: A SUPPLY CHAIN is the network of organizations, resources, activities, and technologies involved in the production and delivery of a product from raw materials to the final customer. Supply chain management issues have become increasingly important to the semiconductor industry due to the global distribution of facilities and its inherent long production time.

subclasses.name: Supply Contract
subclasses.description: A SUPPLY CONTRACT is a formal agreement between two parties—typically a supplier and a buyer—that outlines the terms and conditions under which goods or services will be provided over a specified period. The contract establishes a legally binding relationship and is commonly used in business-to-business transactions.

subclasses.name: Supply Chain
subclasses.description: A SUPPLY CHAIN is the network of organizations, resources, activities, and technologies involved in the production and delivery of a product from raw materials to the final customer. Supply chain management issues have become increasingly important to the semiconductor industry due to the global distribution of facilities and its inherent long production time.

subclasses.name: Delivery Commitment
subclasses.description: DELIVERY COMMITMENT refers to the agreed-upon date or timeframe by which a product, service, or solution is promised to be delivered to a customer. It is a key component of supply chain, project management, and customer service operations, ensuring alignment between supplier capabilities and customer expectations.

subclasses.name: Demand Snapshot
subclasses.description: A DEMAND SNAPSHOT is a fixed capture of demand data at a given point in time. It allows comparison over time or alignment between supply and demand planning cycles.

subclasses.name: Demand Trace
subclasses.description: DEMAND TRACE is the tracking of demand from final customer requests through the supply chain, enabling visibility of demand origins.

subclasses.name: Exchange Rate Specification
subclasses.description: EXCHANGE RATE SPECIFICATION is structured value representing exchange rate.

subclasses.name: Location
subclasses.description:
LOCATION refers to a physical or virtual place where an action, process, or activity occurs, playing a critical role in the execution of tasks within the supply chain, production, and planning systems.

•	Logistics perspective: A location signifies the point where responsibility, ownership, or risk transitions between parties during the transfer of goods or services.
•	Demand Fulfillment Perspective: A location represents the origin or destination of demand-related processes, such as the point of product dispatch, delivery to customers, or storage of inventory to meet customer needs.
•	Planning Perspective: Locations are key inputs for planning activities, representing the physical sites or nodes in the supply chain (e.g., factories, warehouses, or distribution centers) where resources, capacity, or inventory must be allocated.
•	Semiconductor Production Perspective: In manufacturing, a location indicates a specific site where production steps take place, such as fabrication, assembly, or testing.

LOCATIONS are fundamental to managing supply chain efficiency, tracking material flow, coordinating production processes, and ensuring timely fulfillment of customer orders.

subclasses.name: To Location

subclasses.name: Allocation
subclasses.description: ALLOCATION is a process used in supply chain (e.g. order management) in times when demand exceeds available supply.

subclasses.description: CONTACT PERSON DATA refers to the detailed information (name, role, email, phone) of a person responsible for handling specific transactions or communications in the supply chain process.

subclasses.name: Customer Data
subclasses.description: CUSTOMER DATA includes all information necessary to manage orders—such as identifiers, addresses, logistics preferences, and contractual conditions.

subclasses.name: Customer Plant
subclasses.description: A CUSTOMER PLANT refers to the physical location or facility owned or operated by a customer where products, systems, or services are delivered, installed, maintained, or utilized.

subclasses.name: Customer Plant Data
subclasses.description: CUSTOMER PLANT DATA refers to the structured and unstructured information associated with a customer's plant.

subclasses.name: Demand Fulfillment
subclasses.description: DEMAND FULFILLEMENT is the process of meeting a customer´s demand for product or services by fulfilling their request.

subclasses.name: Open Order
subclasses.description: OPEN ORDER refers to a customer order that has been received and recorded in the system but has not yet been fully processed, shipped, or fulfilled. It represents a pending obligation within the sales or supply chain process.

subclasses.name: Open Order Book
subclasses.description: OPEN ORDER BOOK refers to a real-time record of all active, unfulfilled customer orders within an organization. It includes detailed information on sales orders.

subclasses.name: Order Change Request
subclasses.description: An ORDER CHANGE REQUEST is a formal request initiated by a customer or internal stakeholder to modify an existing order after it has been placed but before it is fully fulfilled or invoiced. This request can include changes to product quantities, item specifications, delivery dates, shipping addresses, or other order-related details.

subclasses.name: Order Confirmation
subclasses.description: ORDER CONFIRMATION is a formal acknowledgment from the seller to the customer that an order has been received, reviewed, and accepted under the specified terms and conditions.

subclasses.name: Order Line Item
subclasses.description: An ORDER LINE ITEM is an individual entry within a customer order that specifies the details of a specific product or service being purchased. Each line item represents a unique combination of product, quantity, and pricing, and collectively, line items make up the full contents of an order. A new order line item might be generated when partial fulfillment is committed or delivered.

subclasses.name: In Transit Inventory
subclasses.description: The IN-TRANSIT INVENTORY describes the quantity of a certain product that is shipped from one location to another. This quantity has left the inventory of one location, but has not yet been received into the inventory of the receiving location.

subclasses.name: Inventory
subclasses.description: INVENTORY refers to the stock of goods, materials, and components that a business holds for the purpose of production, resale, or operational use. It is a key asset in supply chain and financial management, directly impacting a company's ability to meet customer demand, manage costs, and generate revenue.

subclasses.name: Inventory Policy
subclasses.description: INVENTORY POLICY is a set of rules that guide how much stock is needed to balance supply with demand. It helps prevent shortages or excess inventory while controlling costs.

This lobes models Application.

subclasses.name: Battery CO2 Savings
subclasses.description: CO2 Savings refers to several solutions that might reduce carbon emissions throughout the course of a Lithiu-Ion battery's lifespan.

subclasses.name: Electric Means Transportation
subclasses.description: Electric_Means_Transportation - refers to vehicles or transportation solutions that leverage electric power systems, predominantly fueled by battery technologies, such as lithium-ion batteries. These systems play a significant role in reducing carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions by eliminating or minimizing the reliance on internal combustion engines (ICEs). With the integration of energy-efficient semiconductors and battery systems, Electric Means Transportation enhances the sustainability of the broader technology and automotive ecosystems.

subclasses.name: Longer Lifespan
subclasses.description: Longer life cycle refers to the number of extra cycles of the battery due good handling throught its lifecycle. It is a way of CO2 savings.

subclasses.name: Optimized Charging
subclasses.description: Second life means that the Lithium-Ion battery has ceased its main activity, in this case powering an electric car, however, it is still able to be used for other purposes.

subclasses.name: Battery Management System
subclasses.description: A battery management system is a set of "electronic control circuits that monitor and regulate the charging and discharge of batteries." It supervises parameters such as the temperature, voltages, capacity, state of charge, power consumption, charging cycles.

subclasses.name: Cells
subclasses.description: Cells are fundamental electrochemical unit, or assembly of electrodes, separators, electrolyte, container, and terminals, that serves as a source of electrical energy by directly converting chemical energy. In this case, the cells are all of the type Li-Ion.

subclasses.name: Functional Block
subclasses.description: A Functional Block is a component of the battery management system.

subclasses.name: Battery Control Unit
subclasses.description: Battery_Control_Unit - is a specialized subclass of Functional_Block, forming a crucial component in systems that manage and control battery performance for sustainable applications. It is an embedded system component responsible for ensuring the safe, efficient, and optimized operation of battery systems, particularly in semiconductor-driven applications.

subclasses.name: Cell Supervision
subclasses.description: Cell_Supervision - is a Functional Block within a battery management system responsible for monitoring individual battery cells' parameters, ensuring their safe operation, and contributing to overall system performance by managing data related to voltage, temperature, and balancing of the cells.

subclasses.name: Current Sensing
subclasses.description: Current_Sensing - is a Functional Block that refers to the process and implementation of measuring electrical current to monitor, regulate, and optimize the performance of an electronic system in a semiconductor supply chain environment.

subclasses.name: Isolated Communication
subclasses.description: Isolated_Communication - is a Functional Block that enables signal transmission between subsystems while maintaining electrical isolation. It is designed for safety, sustainability, and interference resistance in semiconductor-based battery management systems.

subclasses.name: Pack Monitoring
subclasses.description: Pack_Monitoring - a critical role in the semiconductor supply chain as a specialized sustainability feature, enabling real-time tracking and management of battery pack conditions, including temperature distribution, voltage, current, and state-of-health, supporting efficient energy utilization and prolonged battery lifespan.

subclasses.name: Lithium Ion Battery
subclasses.description: The Lithium-Ion Battery represents the set of cells together, which is the battery pack, plus the battery management system.

subclasses.name: Pack
subclasses.description: A battery pack is a set of Lithium-Ion cells.

subclasses.name: Semiconductor
subclasses.description: Semiconductor is an eletronic device which electrical conductivity value is between an insulator and a conductor. In this case, constitutes the battery management system.

subclasses.name: Current Sensor
subclasses.description: Current_Sensor - is a type of semiconductor device used to measure and monitor electrical current flow in a circuit. It is an essential component in the battery management system for ensuring operational efficiency, safety, and sustainability by enabling effective energy flow management and fault detection.

subclasses.name: Magnetic Current Sensor
subclasses.description: A high-precision current sensor for industrial applications based on Infoneon proven Hall technology. The core-less concept significantly reduces footprint compared with existing solutions. Infineon´s TLI4970 is an easy-to-use, fully digital solution that does not require external calibration or additional parts such as A/D converters, 0 pAmps or reference voltage. It thus significantly reduces overall implementation effort as well as PCB space and cost.

subclasses.name: Multichannel Controller Integrated Circuit
subclasses.description: A semiconductor integrated circuit that monitors or controls multiple input or output channels within one device, for example to coordinate several measurements or control paths in a battery management system.

subclasses.name: Power Management Integrated Circuit
subclasses.description: Power_Management_Integrated_Circuit - is a type of semiconductor designed specifically for managing power distribution and energy efficiency in electronic devices or systems. It is integral to battery management, voltage regulation, and the efficient power conversion processes crucial for sustainable and low-energy designs in modern electronics. PMICs play a vital role in the battery management systems by optimizing energy usage and enhancing the lifespan of batteries in portable or renewable energy applications.

subclasses.name: Pressure Sensor
subclasses.description: A semiconductor sensing device that measures pressure and converts the measurement into an electrical signal for monitoring or control, including use in battery management applications.

subclasses.name: UART Transceiver Integrated Circuit
subclasses.description: UART_Transceiver_Integrated_Circuit - is a semiconductor device specifically designed for transmitting and receiving serial data using the Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter (UART) protocol. It operates in battery management systems, facilitating communication between various components, and thereby enhancing the efficiency and reliability of energy management in electronic devices.

subclasses.name: Fieldbus Communication Profile Family
subclasses.description:
A field bus is a bus system that connects field devices such as sensors and actuators in a plant for the purpose of communication with an automation device. If several communication participants send their messages over the same line, then it must be specified who (identifier) says what (measured value, command) and when (initiative). There are standardized protocols for this.
The first generation of fieldbus technology was developed in the 1980s to replace the parallel wiring of binary signals and analog signal transmission that had been common until then with digital transmission technology. Today, many different fieldbus systems with different characteristics are established on the market. Since 1999, fieldbuses have been standardized worldwide in the IEC 61158 standard (Digital data communication for measurement and control - Fieldbus for use in industrial control systems) and by the IEC 61784 standard.
The second generation of fieldbus technology is based on real-time Ethernet (Industrial Ethernet).

A fieldbus defines a complete protocol stack over the 7 layers of the OSI layer model. If necessary, not all layers are occupied.

Example for first generation fieldbus is Profibus,
Example for second generation fieldbus is ProfiNet.

subclasses.name: Digital Factory System
subclasses.description:
The term "Digital Factory" is used in different meanings today and should hence not longer be used.
It should be replaced by more specific terms like "Digital Factory Planning system" or "Digital Factory Twin".
Originally, Digital Factory referred to software tools for computer-aided planning, design, engineering and simulation of production, manufacturing, or assembly systems. These tools supplemented CAD-based tools for factory layout planning and tools for computer-aided tools for production engineering (work plan preparation, production process planning) and were glued together with them to PLM software suites.
As today even CAD-based layout planning and process planning tools are "digital" and refer to the factory, the terms "Digital Factory tool" and "Production Engineering tool" more and more converge.
At the same time, automation vendors start to use the concept "Digital Factory" to address online monitoring and control tools for production systems. In this meaning, the term is a synonym for "Digital Factory Twin" or "Digital Twin of a Factory".
The important difference between these two meanings is the phase in the life cycle in which the tool is used: Manufacturing Planning / Eingineering is conducted mainly in the first two lifecycle phases in which the product (type, class) is created, designed, and engineered, as well as the corresponding production system.
The online monitoring and control is conducted during the third phase, in which the product individuals are produced on the existing production system.
Hartwig Baumgaertel, 2018-11-12
